author: dug-21
body:
## Summary
Wires rmcp's Streamable-HTTP `allowed_hosts` host-allowlist from `UNIMATRIX_PUBLIC_URL`, fixing `403 Forbidden: Host header is not allowed` for remote clients connecting over direct container HTTPS by their configured public hostname.

Fixes #774.

## Root cause
`McpAdapter::new` set `config.allowed_origins` but left `config.allowed_hosts` at rmcp's localhost-only default. `PublicUrl.sans` — which already contains the configured public host plus the local SANs — was available at the wiring site but dropped, because the constructor chain (`from_servers` → `from_server` → `McpAdapter::new`) only threaded `allowed_origins`. This left the R-09 "single derivation, three consumers" invariant satisfied for only 2 of 3 consumers (cert SAN ✅, bundle base_url ✅, allowed_hosts ❌).

## Fix
- Thread `allowed_hosts: Vec<String>` (= `public_url.sans`) alongside `allowed_origins` through the constructor chain, mirroring the vnc-023/ADR-002 additive-param pattern; set `config.allowed_hosts` in `McpAdapter::new`.
- Add `debug_assert!(!allowed_hosts.is_empty())` at the `main.rs` wiring site — rmcp treats an empty `allowed_hosts` as allow-all (fail-open), and `allowed_hosts`/`allowed_origins` share constructor params with opposite empty-semantics, so the guard prevents a future refactor silently failing open.
- Rewrite the now-stale `router.rs` comment to document the wiring and the empty=fail-open hazard.

`.sans` is structurally non-empty (≥3 local SANs even when `UNIMATRIX_PUBLIC_URL` is unset), so the unset case stays localhost-only and the CVE-2026-42559 posture is preserved. Single-host contract, consistent with cert SAN + bundle base_url.

## Tests
- `test_adapter_allows_configured_public_host_rejects_others` — host-gate regression: configured public host clears the gate, unrelated host 403s.
- `test_unset_public_url_yields_non_empty_allowed_hosts` — fail-open guard: unset still yields a restrictive localhost-only allowlist.
- `test_portless_allowed_host_matches_host_with_port` — rmcp port-less-matches-any-port semantic.

## Validation
- Workspace: 6422 passed / 0 failed. Integration smoke: 24/24. Bug-relevant suites: 207 passed / 1 pre-existing xfail (GH#405).
- `unimatrix-server` clippy clean. (Pre-existing workspace clippy debt in `unimatrix-observe`/`unimatrix-engine` is tracked by GH#756/#688 and untouched here.)
- Bugfix gate: PASS (7/7).

---

## 2026-06-17: Mastra npm Supply Chain Attack: Auditing and Hardening Your AI Agent Framework Dependencies

**Suggested slug:** `mastra-npm-supply-chain-response`
**Status:** pending research

### Why this topic, why now

On June 17, 2026, attackers pulled off the first documented scope-level npm takeover targeting an AI agent framework. A dormant contributor account (inactive 16 months, access never revoked) was hijacked, and 144 malicious @mastra package versions were published in an 88-minute automated campaign. The payload was hidden inside easy-day-js, a typosquatted copy of the popular dayjs library, which ran a postinstall dropper that exfiltrated LLM API keys, crypto wallet data, CI/CD secrets, and browser credentials before self-deleting. Mastra's @mastra/core package alone has 918,000+ weekly downloads, with 29M+ accumulated monthly downloads across the scope. The incident is now resolved (malicious versions unpublished), but zero practitioner guides exist explaining how to check if your AI project was hit, what to rotate, or how to block this class of attack going forward.

### Search demand evidence

- [Mastra compromised in supply chain attack](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48565319) - Hacker News discussion thread (posted June 17, 2026)
- [144 Mastra npm Packages Compromised via Hijacked Contributor Account](https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/144-mastra-npm-packages-compromised-via.html) - The Hacker News (cybersecurity), June 2026
- [A Forgotten Contributor Account Compromised the Entire Mastra npm Package Scope](https://snyk.io/blog/a-forgotten-contributor-account-compromised-the-entire-mastra-npm-package-scope/) - Snyk, June 2026. Technical analysis of the SLSA attestation gap that let unsigned packages through.
- [INCIDENT REPORT: 2026-06-16: Mastra hit by supply-chain attack](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/issues/18061) - Official Mastra incident report on GitHub
- [140+ Mastra npm Packages Compromised in Coordinated Supply Chain Attack](https://socket.dev/blog/mastra-npm-packages-compromised) - Socket.dev, June 2026
- [Mastra npm Supply Chain Attack: 140+ Packages Backdoored via easy-day-js Typosquat](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mastra-npm-packages-compromised-using-easy-day-js) - StepSecurity, June 2026. Notes that enforcing SLSA provenance verification would have blocked every malicious package in this campaign.

### Competition check

Searching "Mastra npm attack response guide" and "how to audit AI framework dependencies after supply chain attack" returns only news reporting (The Hacker News, CybersecurityNews, CyberPress, SC Media, SecurityOnline) and vendor analyses (Snyk, Socket, StepSecurity, OX Security, Aikido). Every piece describes what happened. None walk a developer through the full response: checking lockfiles for affected versions, determining whether the postinstall dropper ran on your machine or CI runners, rotating LLM API keys across every provider connected through Mastra, and setting up npm audit signatures plus SLSA attestation verification to catch unsigned packages before they install. The blog's existing `litellm-mcp-exploit-response-guide` establishes the incident-response content pattern, and the audience overlaps directly - AI engineers building with JavaScript/TypeScript agent frameworks are the same developers reading about LiteLLM and MCP security.

### Suggested next step

`/research-topic "mastra-npm-supply-chain-response"` to produce the full content brief with keyword strategy, FAQ candidates, and outline.

author: kdeyarmin
body:
## Why

Follow-up to the Codex P2 review on #1079 (now merged). Migration `0383` grants the platform super-admin tier (`resupply.platform_admins`) **by email in a single shot**. In a brand-new environment where `kdeyarmin@comcast.net` doesn't exist yet, that `WHERE` matches nothing, the migrator records 0383 as applied, and it never re-runs — so an owner bootstrapped *later* would never get the grant and couldn't pass `/resupply-api/platform/me`.

(Production is unaffected — that account already exists and is already a platform admin via migration 0355.)

## What

Move the grant into the **order-correct** path:

- New **`--platform-admin`** flag on `auth:bootstrap-admin`. After the auth user row is guaranteed to exist (just created or found), it idempotently upserts `resupply.platform_admins` (`onConflict: auth_user_id, ignoreDuplicates`). Requires `--role=admin` (the platform tier is admin-only).

```
pnpm --filter @workspace/scripts auth:bootstrap-admin \
  --email=owner@example.com --role=admin --platform-admin
```

Migration `0383` is left in place (it's merged + immutable per ADR 003) and still serves as the best-effort immediate grant for in-place upgrades where the account already exists.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @workspace/scripts typecheck` passes; Prettier clean.
- The grant is idempotent (safe to re-run) and only fires with the explicit flag, so existing bootstrap behavior is unchanged.

## What this adds

A looping background **song on the main menu page only**.

- Extracted the audio from the uploaded clip to `menu-music.mp3` (~480 KB) so only the sound loads, not the video.

author: mrnzdev
body:
## Summary
Adds five high-value notifications for events that previously fired silently, plus notification-panel UX/quality improvements. Builds on the existing queued `database` + `broadcast` (Reverb) notification system.

### New notifications
| Notification | Trigger | Recipient |
|---|---|---|
| Join request created | someone requests to join a team | team leaders |
| Invitation accepted | invitee accepts (success path only) | the inviter |
| Captaincy transferred | captaincy handed over | the new captain |
| Match confirmed | home leader accepts a request | home team leaders (away already notified) |
| Tournament registration reviewed | organizer approves/rejects | registering team's leaders |

Each follows the existing pattern: queued, `database` + `broadcast`, Spanish copy, deep-linked `action_url`.

### UX & quality
- **Date grouping** in the dropdown (Hoy / Ayer / Anteriores) with sticky headers.
- **Sound on real-time push** (Web Audio chime, never on the polling fallback) + **unread count in the browser tab title**.
- **Brand-green color pass**: affirmative events lean into the palette green (emerald/green/teal/lime); negatives stay red/orange; unread indicators (bell badge, row border/tint, dot) now use the primary green.
- **Bug fix (419):** notification writes now send the live `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie instead of the stale `<meta name="csrf-token">`, which broke mark-read / delete / clear after the session token rotated.

## Tests
- New `tests/Feature/NewNotificationsTest.php` (7 tests) asserts each notification reaches the right recipients and not the actor.
- Full suite green: **345 passed**. `tsc` clean, Pint + Prettier clean.

## Not included (follow-ups)
Member removed/left, match details-changed, match completed, low-availability alerts, tournament lifecycle changes, and a notification **preferences** system.

## 概要

Next.js stack pack に「認知 → **強制** → **検知**」の強制層・検知層を新設する。これで下流の Next.js PJ は **opt-in 一発で golden path に乗り（scaffold）・地図が描け（system-map）・違反が CI で止まる（fitness）** が揃う。

fitness（契約）と scaffold（生成器）は **契約と生成器の関係**で、`scaffold/template/` が fitness の conforming fixture を兼ねるため、scaffold 出力 ≡ fitness green が物理的に保証され**ドリフト不能**。

## 中身

### `fitness-functions/`（検知層・依存ゼロ plain Node）
- `lib/route-enumerator.js` — 正準カウントの**単一定義**（route/screen/server-action/cron/mutation 面を凍結。数え方ぶれ 87/88/92/93/112 を解消）。fitness と後続の system-map route adapter が同参照（DRY）。
- `checks.js` — S1-S7 / H1 / H3 / H4 を `ARCHITECTURE.md` の grep assertion どおりに実装。`error=HARD / warn=SOFT 残差`。**文字列・正規表現リテラル保護付き comment-strip** で checker 自身の誤検知・false-negative を防止（methodology の「コメント≠一次ソース」を checker にも適用）。escape hatch `// barrel-ok` `// authz-ok`。
- `run-fitness.js`（CI 主・WSL 安全な単一プロセス・error で exit 1）/ `verify.js`（自己検証）/ `templates/architecture.test.ts`（vitest 代替）/ `fixtures/violations/*`（各ルールの反例）/ `README.md`。

### `scaffold/`（強制層）
- `template/` = 規約を満たす具体 `posts` 縦スライス（全 MUST を1スライスで体現・= fitness の conforming fixture と同一ファイル）。
- `scaffold.js`（verbatim 展開 + `gitignore`→`.gitignore`）/ `README.md`。

### doc
`ARCHITECTURE.md` 強制節 / pack `README.md` roadmap（fitness・scaffold ✅）/ system-map adapters README に正準 enumerator の単一定義を明記 / `CHANGELOG`。

## 検証（self-verified・実走）
- `verify.js`: **conforming = error 0 / warn 0**、全 violation fixture で該当ルール発火、正準カウント凍結。
- **scaffold → fitness roundtrip = 0/0**。
- system-map self-verify PASS（無改変・回帰なし）。
- **敵対的レビュー（5レンズ・経験的バイパス検証）**の must-fix 5件 + 安価な honesty/correctness 修正を反映済み（regex-literal strip / S4 inline をインデント非依存化 / 正準カウント凍結 / Next 16 の eslint 移行 / soft-delete `$extends` 完全化 / S2 type-only 除外＋dynamic 検出 等。回帰防止 fixture 同梱）。
- PII scan clean。

## スコープ
opt-in pack 内のみ（`STACK_PACK=nextjs`）。非 Next PJ 無影響・ccs core 不変。次は検証下流 PJ への dogfood。

### Motivation
- Create a clean render adapter boundary so the Crystal Wand Day Capsule payload can be handed to a renderer later without hardcoding fake images or locking to a provider.
- Ensure provider safety by keeping any external image provider calls behind a backend boundary and by returning an explicit renderer-not-connected state from the frontend when no renderer exists.

### Description
- Added a new service `src/services/dayCapsuleRenderService.js` that exposes `buildDayCapsuleRenderRequest`, `requestDayCapsuleRender`, `getDayCapsuleRenderStatus`, `normalizeDayCapsuleRenderResult`, and `persistDayCapsuleRender` and persists render records to client storage using `localStorage` keys.
- Defined a render request model that includes `renderId`, `payloadId`, `dayIdentity`, `assuredThoughts` (diary + two Penny Q&A), `sourceSnapshot` (mood, wordOfDay, headHummer, era, singlenessLevel, moments, THICC/Remember.Me/THICC.FITT/DA.EATER signals, otherSignals), `renderInstructions`, `revision`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt`.
- Implemented a render status model and constants (`idle`, `ready_to_render`, `renderer_not_connected`, `queued`, `rendering`, `rendered`, `revision_requested`, `revised`, `failed`) and a normalization layer for persisted records and artifacts.
- Connected THE.SUMMATION UI (`components/sections/TheSummationSection.jsx`) to the adapter so the Wand payload becomes a render request, persisted render status is read, the UI shows status-specific messages (including “Renderer not connected yet. Day Capsule payload is ready.”) and only renders an artifact preview when a real `renderArtifact.url` exists; no fake images or API keys are added.

### Testing
- Ran a production build with `npm run build`, which completed successfully and prerendered static pages.
- Verified the app compiles without runtime errors and the THE.SUMMATION render zone now shows persisted render status and the renderer-not-connected placeholder when no renderer is attached.

author: actorjoon0001-glitch
body:
## 증상
다른 컴퓨터에서 **3D 화면으로 전환하면 우측 사이드바(속성 패널)가 사라짐**

## 원인
`viewer3d.js`의 `_resize()`가 `renderer.setSize(w, h, false)`로 호출 — `updateStyle=false`라 **캔버스의 CSS 표시 크기를 설정하지 않음**. 그 결과 캔버스 표시 크기가 드로잉버퍼 크기(= 너비 × `devicePixelRatio`)가 됨.
- 개발 PC: `devicePixelRatio = 1` → 정상
- 고해상도(Retina 등) PC: `devicePixelRatio = 2` → 캔버스가 **2배로 커져** 우측 사이드바를 뷰포트 밖으로 밀어내고, `body { overflow:hidden }`에 잘려 사라짐
- 2D는 `#canvas2d { width:100% }`로 묶여 있어 멀쩡 → "3D일 때만" 증상과 일치

## 수정
- **`src/viewer3d.js`**: `setSize(w, h, true)`로 변경 — 캔버스 CSS 크기를 컨테이너에 맞춤 (three.js 표준 사용법)
- **`styles/app.css`**: 안전장치로 `.view3d canvas`에 `width/height:100% !important`, `.stage`·`.view3d`에 `overflow:hidden` 추가 → 어떤 경우에도 캔버스가 사이드바를 덮지 않음

## 검증
- `viewer3d.js` 문법 검사 통과
- 레이아웃에 `@media` 쿼리 없음 확인(반응형 숨김 아님) → 캔버스 오버플로가 유일 원인

※ 이 환경엔 고해상도 디스플레이가 없어 육안 재현은 불가하나, 표준 사용법 + CSS 강제 제약으로 컨테이너를 넘지 않도록 이중으로 보장했습니다.

author: crypto2099
body:
`/prepare` validates grids (validateGrid in ballot.ts: integers, step > 0, max >= min, (max - min) % step === 0). But the ballot is fetched from IPFS at /start (and on session rehydration) and trusted as-is — it is never re-validated — so a malformed grid can reach the tally.

The concrete danger is `gridValues`, which enumerates the grid with `for (v = min; v <= max; v += step)`. A non-positive `step` makes that loop never terminate: finalize hangs on an unbounded array. (The vote-path `isOnGrid` is already fail-closed in JS — `x % 0` is NaN, `NaN === 0` is false — so a malformed grid there rejects values rather than panicking. The tally enumeration is the real exposure.)

Guard `gridValues`: reject a grid whose min/max/step are not integers, or with step <= 0, max < min, or (max - min) not divisible by step, by throwing instead of looping. The throw is raised inside `tallyVotes`, which runs inside each settle route's outer try/catch, so finalize returns an error response instead of hanging.

Files:
- src/routes/settlement.ts — gridValues validates its grid and throws on a malformed spec; exported so it can be unit-tested.
- tests/f003-gridspec-validation.test.ts — well-formed grids enumerate; step=0, negative step, max<min, non-integer bound/step, indivisible range, NaN/Infinity all throw rather than hang.

body:
## Summary
- Align `get_session_next_ready()` with the documented ready-task contract: task `priority` ascending first, then `created_at`, then `id`.
- Reuse the same Cypher ordering fragment for broad ready-task listing, session next-ready, project ready-work, and wake-on-transition readiness.
- Strengthen `tests/ready_definition_acceptance.py` with mixed plan/direct and cross-project fixtures so reverting to project-priority-first ordering fails.
- Refresh docs that describe task priority as lower-number-first.

## Root Cause
`taey-plan next` ultimately calls `get_session_next_ready()`, whose query sorted by `proj.priority` before `t.priority`. A higher-priority task in a lower-ranked project could lose to a lower-priority task in another project, while `taey-task list` was task-priority-first. Direct `taey-task` tasks are parented under the default project/phase, so they were included in `next-ready` but ranked under project priority as well.

## 背景

启用 aster-api 的 trial guard（k3s `ASTER_SECURITY_EVALUATE_SOURCE_TRIAL=true`，修 playground 的 plan-gate `api_access_denied`）后，playground Run 改报 **`origin_not_allowed`**。

## 根因

本 playground BFF 的 server→server fetch（→ aster-api `/evaluate-source`）**从不转发 `Origin` 头**，只发 `X-Tenant-Id` / `X-User-Role` / HMAC `signedHeaders`。

trial guard 此前 `disabled` 时不查 Origin，所以这个 gap 没暴露。一旦 `enabled`，`TrialEndpointGuard` 的 Origin allowlist 校验拿不到 Origin → `origin_not_allowed`。

## 改动

把**已通过本 BFF allowlist 校验**的 browser Origin 转发给 aster-api（其 allowlist 镜像本 BFF：`aster-lang.dev` / `.cloud`）。

**安全**：Origin 不在 HMAC 签名的 canonical（`method|path|timestamp`）内，转发不破坏内部 caller 验签。且只在 `origin` 已清过本 BFF allowlist 后才到达此处。

## 验证

tsc / eslint 绿。配合 aster-api trial guard 启用 + Flyway 修复（pod 已 6/6 健康），playground 可匿名执行。

Auditability hardening on top of the v0.14 proof baseline
(`mvp2-v0.14-learning-proven-isaac-eval`). **No closure numbers or claim
boundaries change** — this only makes the review package harder to forge.

Closes two gaps found in adversarial review of the verifier:

The frozen closure gate records only 6 of the 8 non-claims; marketplace and
production readiness previously lived only in the unprotected manifest. This
PR adds **`data/non_claims_attestation.json`** — all 8 non-claims false,

author: alexander-turner
body:
## Problem

Hard-refreshing `turntrout.com/design` (or any long page) while scrolled partway down caused the desktop ToC to highlight the **first** entry instead of the section you were actually at.

## Root cause

The `IntersectionObserver` uses `rootMargin: "0px 0px -70% 0px"`, so a heading only counts as "active" while sitting in the **top 30%** of the viewport. On a fresh load that lands mid-page, no heading is inside that narrow band. The observer callback was gated behind `visibleSections.size > 0`, so it did nothing — leaving the active link stuck on the `firstSectionId` seed value set at init.

## Fix

`quartz/components/scripts/toc.inline.ts`

- Added `getActiveSectionByScroll()`: when the detection band is empty, resolves to the **last heading scrolled above the band** (the section you're reading).
- Added `resolveActiveSection()`: uses the observer's `visibleSections` when populated, otherwise falls back to `getActiveSectionByScroll()`.
- Both the observer callback and the init path now call `resolveActiveSection()`.

## Tests

Added a Playwright regression test (`Re-initializing while scrolled past the detection band highlights the passed heading`) that:

1. Scrolls to page bottom so all headings are above the detection band.
2. Asserts `headingsInBand === 0` — proving the fallback, not the observer, drives the result.
3. Fires a `nav` event (simulating a fresh load) and waits for the active link to match the heading we scrolled past.
4. Guards that `expectedSlug !== firstSlug` so the test is only meaningful when the page actually has multiple headings.

Verified the test **fails** against the pre-fix bundle and **passes** with the fix applied.

author: ggdouglas
body:
Second of three PRs splitting up #8065, stacked on #8174. Adds the `@blueprintjs/icons/next` entrypoint and the static icon components consumers import directly.

## What's here

This adds a second icon pipeline next to the legacy one, with its own SVG sources, generator, generated tree, and published subpath. This makes it so that each icon (e.g. `import { AirplaneIcon } from "@blueprintjs/icons/next"`) resolves to a static, tree-shakeable React component. It also adds a small legacy→next name-map utility for migration tooling.  No runtime or dynamic loading components are included here; that's deliberate these are included in a subsequent PR (#8177).

### The `@blueprintjs/icons/next` subpath

A nested `next/` entry (`next/package.json` + `next/index.d.ts`) makes the subpath resolve to the compiled generated tree. The type barrel lives physically at `next/index.d.ts` (rather than being a pure `package.json` redirect) so TypeScript auto-import emits the canonical `@blueprintjs/icons/next` specifier instead of a deep `lib/esm/next/generated` path. Runtime JS resolves via `main`/`module`; types resolve via `.d.ts`.

### Static components

A new generator (`scripts/generate-next-icon-components.mjs`) reads the next SVG sources and writes one self-contained `.tsx` per icon, with the path data inlined as a `const` and a named export. Outlined icons export `<Name>Icon`; icons that also have a filled style export `<Name>FilledIcon` as well. Each component renders into `SvgIconContainerNext`, a thin `<svg>` wrapper (close to the legacy `SVGIconContainer`) that takes its color from `currentColor` and its size from a `size` prop.

The generated tree (`src/next/generated/`, gitignored and produced at build time) contains:

- `components/*.tsx` - one module per icon/variant (`<Name>Icon`, plus `<Name>FilledIcon` where a filled variant exists)
- `components/index.ts` - a flat barrel re-exporting every component
- `manifest.ts` - `icons-next.json` validated and re-emitted as a typed const (`nextIconManifest`), plus the `BlueprintIconsNext` string-literal union (aliased as `IconNextName`) and `NextIconManifestEntry` type, which back search and the gallery
- `index.ts` - the package barrel for the `/next` subpath (components + manifest + container + a re-export of the main `@blueprintjs/icons` entry)

### How this differs from the legacy static pipeline

The legacy pipeline encodes size as two path sets in one component (separate 16px and 20px grids, switched at render time). The next pipeline encodes style as two separate components (outlined and filled), both drawn on a single 16px grid and scaled by the `size` prop. The two share the same overall shape (resources → generator → gitignored generated tree → `tsc` → `lib` → published entry), but the next one keeps its own source set, generated namespace, and subpath.

### Name-map utility

`getIconNextName()` / `LegacyToIconNextNameMap` (generated from `icons-name-map.json`) translate a legacy icon name to its next-generation equivalent (e.g. `add` → `circle-plus`). This is what a migration codemod can consume to rewrite legacy icon references.

### Verification

The `icons:verify` script now also checks `icons-next.json` and `icons-name-map.json` against the SVGs on disk: manifest entries are well-formed, `hasFilled` matches what's actually on disk, the manifest and the outlined directory line up both ways, every filled icon has an outlined counterpart, and every legacy icon maps to a real next icon.

## Stack

0. Base PR (#8065)
1. assets + manifests (#8174)
2. **(this PR)** static icon components
3. static icon docs (#8182)
4. dynamic `IconNext` component (#8177)

author: sobradob
body:
Closes BOA-120.

Export is slow, and the **first** export of a session is the worst — exactly when a new user is deciding whether the product is worth it. This addresses both levers from the issue plus the instrumentation to confirm the win.

## What changed

**1. Default to Instagram portrait** — new IG portrait preset (`183×229mm @150 DPI` ≈ **1081×1352 px, exactly 4:5**) and a `DEFAULT_PRESET` the editor opens on. **~2.86× fewer pixels** than the old 30×40 free export (1.46 MP vs 4.19 MP): less to rasterize server-side, fewer basemap tiles, smaller output.

**2. Cheaper/faster digital file (JPEG)** — free exports re-encode as **JPEG q0.9** instead of PNG via `applyWatermark`, the single chokepoint all three render paths (server / capture / canvas) flow through. A ~1080×1350 JPEG is a few hundred KB vs multi-MB PNG — the literal "faster to load/share" win. Prints are untouched (rendered clean server-side, never watermarked). The server render engine/routes are deliberately left alone.

**3. Kill the first-export cold start** — the editor fires a fire-and-forget `GET /api/render/health` on mount (gated on `RENDER_ON_SERVER`) to warm Chromium before the first export click.

**4. Keep print ordering one-tap** — a digital canvas now auto-selects the `30×40` (`a4-poster`) tier so **"Order Print" stays enabled** (with a "reframed to print proportions" note) instead of dead-ending the paid funnel. Per product decision.

**5. Instrumentation** — `export_completed` now carries `render_ms`, `size`, `output_px`, `format`, `first_export` (session-first / cold), and `file_bytes`, so cold-vs-warm-by-size is queryable in Mixpanel.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Default export size is Instagram (portrait).
- [x] Print-resolution export remains selectable; ordering still works one-tap.
- [x] Export render time instrumented (cold vs warm, by size).
- [ ] First-export latency materially closer to warm — prewarm shipped; **needs production measurement** via the new events to set a target (heavier prewarm deferred until data shows the gap isn't just Chromium launch).

## Files
- `src/types/poster.ts` — IG portrait preset + `DEFAULT_PRESET`
- `src/features/poster/infrastructure/renderer/watermark.ts` — `applyWatermark(blob, { type, quality })`, PNG default (back-compat)
- `src/features/poster/ui/PosterEditor.tsx` — default size, JPEG paths, `.jpg` filename, prewarm, instrumentation
- `src/features/checkout/ui/OrderButton.tsx` — auto-pick print tier from a digital size
- `src/features/poster/ui/SettingsPanel.tsx` — "Export Image (Free)" label

## Verification
- `npm run build` (tsc strict + vite) green.
- `npm run lint` — no new errors on touched files (only the pre-existing `posterConfig: any` in OrderButton, untouched).
- Numeric: IG free export = 1081×1352 px (1.46 MP), aspect 0.800 = 4:5.
- ⚠️ **Browser smoke not yet run** — the preview launcher fails with `EPERM: uv_cwd` (sandbox cwd issue in the worktree, unrelated to the change). Needs a manual pass: editor opens at 4:5, free export downloads a `.jpg`, Order Print enabled by default and orders 30×40.

author: binbinao
body:
## Summary
Closes #3 — addresses the "AuthService.parseIdTokenClaims 跳过 Azure AD id_token 签名校验" CRITICAL finding from the 2026-06-17 code review (Backend C-4).

`AuthService.java:145-157` parsed id_token claims via `JWTUtil.parseToken(idToken).getPayloads()` without verifying the signature. The source code's own comment acknowledged this: "Production hardening: verify signature against Microsoft JWKS (jwks_uri)". Without the check, any caller with network access to `/api/v1/auth/callback` could submit a self-signed id_token for any email and have the server issue a LIMS JWT for that email.

## Changes
- **`lims-service/src/main/java/com/lims/service/AuthService.java`**:
  - Switch from `cn.hutool.jwt.JWTUtil` to nimbus-jose-jwt (`SignedJWT` + `JWKSet` + `RSASSAVerifier`).
  - New `loadJwks()` method fetches `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenantId}/discovery/v2.0/keys` via the existing `RestTemplate`, with a 10-minute in-memory TTL.
  - `parseIdTokenClaims` now: (1) parses the JWS, (2) finds the JWK by `kid`, (3) verifies the RS256 signature, (4) checks `iss == https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenantId}/v2.0`, (5) checks `aud` contains the configured `clientId`, (6) checks `exp` is in the future, (7) checks `nbf` (if present) is not in the future. Any failure raises `BusinessException(M365_INTEGRATION_ERROR)`.
- **`lims-service/src/test/java/com/lims/service/AuthServiceIdTokenVerificationTest.java`** (new): 4 JUnit tests covering all four contracts (JWKS import present, iss checked against microsoftonline.com, aud checked, exp checked). Source-level structural tests — a heavier behavioural test (mocked JWKS provider + real RSA key pair) is documented as follow-up.

## TDD cycle
- **RED** — wrote the test first. Confirmed all 4 failed:
  - `authServiceImportsJwksClassForSignatureVerification` — no nimbus imports
  - `authServiceValidatesIdTokenIssuerClaim` — no iss check
  - `authServiceValidatesIdTokenAudienceClaim` — no aud check
  - `authServiceValidatesIdTokenExpirationClaim` — no exp check
- **GREEN** — refactored `parseIdTokenClaims` to verify + validate. All 4 tests now pass: `Tests run: 4, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0`.

## Verification
```
$ JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@17/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home \
  ./mvnw clean test -pl lims-service -am -Dtest=AuthServiceIdTokenVerificationTest \
  -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false
...
[INFO] Tests run: 4, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
[INFO] BUILD SUCCESS
```

## Operational impact
- `parseIdTokenClaims` now requires network access to `login.microsoftonline.com` to fetch JWKS on first call or after TTL expiry (10 min). Subsequent calls within 10 min use the cached JWK set.
- A forged id_token (self-signed) or one with wrong `iss` / `aud` / `exp` will throw `BusinessException(M365_INTEGRATION_ERROR)` — `handleCallback` will surface a 400 to the client.
- nimbus-jose-jwt is on the classpath transitively (via `microsoft-graph` / `msal4j`); no `pom.xml` change needed. (We could add it as a direct dep for explicitness — happy to follow up if you'd like.)

body:
### Motivation

- Prevent user-authored callout labels from injecting Markdown/callout structure or leaking lines into output by normalizing and escaping labels.
- Avoid emitting dangerous Markdown links by adding an explicit safe-href policy that preserves visible text while dropping unsafe wrappers.
- Ensure plain paragraph text cannot accidentally become headings, lists, quotes, or thematic breaks by adding line-start escaping.
- Add focused and golden tests to lock down the exporter behavior for future reviews and corpus handoffs.

### Description

- Normalized and escaped callout labels via a new `calloutLabel` helper that collapses whitespace/newlines, trims, and applies `escapeMarkdownText` before using it in the callout marker. (modified `serializeCallout` to use `calloutLabel`).
- Made inline escaping line-aware by adding `escapeMarkdownLineStart` and updating `escapeMarkdownText` to protect heading markers, quote markers, list and ordered-list markers, and thematic-break candidates. 
- Replaced the previous `linkHref` behavior with `safeMarkdownHref` and `escapeMarkdownHref` to allow anchors, repo-relative/root-relative paths, `http`/`https`, and `mailto`, while rejecting protocol-relative links, control characters, and unsafe schemes (javascript:, data:, file:, etc.); unsafe links are degraded to plain visible text. 
- Preserved existing mark serialization behavior (code exclusivity, bold/italic/strike rules, outermost link wrapping) while swapping to the new safe href helper and added a set of focused unit tests plus a golden export test. 
- Files changed: `apps/live-control-ui/src/tiptap/markdown/calloutMarkdown.ts` and `apps/live-control-ui/src/tiptap/markdown/calloutMarkdown.test.ts`.

### Testing

- Ran the focused tests with `npm --prefix apps/live-control-ui run test -- --run src/tiptap/markdown/calloutMarkdown.test.ts` and all 23 tests passed. 
- Ran the full test suite with `npm --prefix apps/live-control-ui run test` where most suites passed but 3 suites could not load because this environment could not resolve `@tiptap/react` (package-resolution issue observed). 
- Attempted build with `npm --prefix apps/live-control-ui run build` and the build/checks were blocked by the same unresolved `@tiptap` packages (`@tiptap/react`, `@tiptap/starter-kit`, `@tiptap/core`) in this environment.

author: drdave-flexnetos
body:
## PHTASK-0051 — Complete chaos-automation scheduler + real webhook POST

Completes the hollow chaos-automation feature in `prompt-hub/src/chaos_auto.rs`. The manual `run_chaos`/trend/alert core was already real; this wires the scheduler to it and makes webhook alerts perform a genuine HTTP POST.

### Before
- **Scheduler (`spawn_task`)**: only ticked and logged `"Chaos auto-scheduler tick completed"`, then discarded the hub with `let _ = hub;` — it **never called `run_chaos`**. A comment even admitted "The scheduler task does not execute chaos runs directly here."
- **Webhook action**: `AlertAction::Webhook(url)` only emitted `warn!("Webhook alert (placeholder): would POST to {}", url)` — no HTTP request was ever made.

### After
- `spawn_task` sources the hub's `ChaosEngine`, builds a self-contained `'static` execution context (cloned engine + schedule + alert config), and on **every tick runs the real chaos engine** via a new shared `run_once` core, maintains a bounded rolling history for trend tracking, and dispatches alerts on degradation.
- New **`spawn_scheduler_with`** (the testable scheduler core): accepts an injected interval, an executor factory (one executor minted per tick so the `FnMut` need not be `Clone`), and an optional `TickHook` observer — so a test proves the engine fired per tick without real wall-clock waits.
- Extracted **`dispatch_alerts`** (shared by `run_chaos` and the scheduler) and **`post_webhook`**, which performs a **real `reqwest` POST** of a JSON payload (`run_id`, timestamps, `overall_pass_rate`, trigger, strategy count) and maps transport errors / non-2xx into `HubError::Network`. Alert dispatch is best-effort: a failed POST is logged and never aborts the run.
- `chaos-automation` now enables the **already-present** optional `reqwest` dep (shared with `local-llm`/`qdrant`) — **no new dependency added**.

### reqwest
`reqwest` was **already a dependency** (optional, used by `qdrant.rs` and `local_llm.rs`). The only change is enabling it for the `chaos-automation` feature: `chaos-automation = ["chaos", "dep:reqwest"]`. No new HTTP crate introduced; matched the existing `reqwest::Client` idiom and `HubError::Network` error model.

### Tests added (in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`)
- `scheduler_fires_run_chaos_at_interval` — injects a 10ms interval + an atomic `TickHook` counter, asserts the real engine produced ≥3 valid records (bounded await, no wall-clock dependency).
- `webhook_action_issues_real_post` — stands up a oneshot TCP listener as a minimal HTTP server, dispatches an `AlertAction::Webhook`, and asserts the captured request is `POST /alert` with a JSON body carrying the run's `overall_pass_rate` and `run_id`.

### Gate evidence (mise stripped, toolchain pinned to 1.96.0)
```
cargo build  -p prompt-hub                                    # Finished, OK
cargo build  -p prompt-hub --features chaos-automation        # Finished (reqwest links), OK
cargo test   -p prompt-hub --features chaos-automation chaos  # 18 passed (lib) + 4 passed (integration), 0 failed
  ...incl. chaos_auto::tests::scheduler_fires_run_chaos_at_interval ... ok
  ...incl. chaos_auto::tests::webhook_action_issues_real_post ... ok
cargo clippy -p prompt-hub --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo fmt    -p prompt-hub --check                            # clean
```
Note: the `chaos` module is feature-gated, so `cargo test chaos` without `--features chaos-automation` filters all chaos tests out (matches the existing repo design — `tests/test_chaos_auto.rs` is itself `#[cfg(feature = "chaos-automation")]`). The new tests run under that feature; clippy `--all-features` covers the new code.

### Scope
Touched only `prompt-hub/src/chaos_auto.rs` (per path_scope) and `prompt-hub/Cargo.toml` (one-line feature edit to enable the already-present `reqwest` for the webhook POST — unavoidable, called out above). No `hub.rs` change was needed: `spawn_task`'s existing signature `(&self, hub: &PromptHub)` was sufficient.

No new stubs / `todo!()` / placeholders.

author: r6e
body:
## Summary

Adds the OPA builtins `uri.parse` and `uri.is_valid`. Both are thin wrappers over Go's `net/url.Parse`; Ruby's stdlib `URI` diverges fundamentally (stricter, lacks Go's RawPath/host quirks), so this is a faithful from-scratch port of `net/url`:

- `uri.parse(s)` → the components OPA exposes (`scheme`, `hostname`, `port`, `path`, `raw_path`, `raw_query`, `fragment`), each only when non-empty; `raw_path` is `cmp.Or(RawPath, Path)`. userinfo and the opaque component are dropped, matching OPA.
- `uri.is_valid(s)` → whether `net/url.Parse` succeeds (`false` for a non-string or the empty string, per OPA).

The port covers `getScheme`, `parse`, `parseAuthority`, `parseHost` (incl. the current Go 1.26 `netip` IPv6-literal validation — non-empty-zone enforcement, IPv4-mapped acceptance), `setPath`'s RawPath invariant, `unescape`/`escape` per encoding mode, the host/port last-colon split, userinfo/opaque branches, and the exact error/undefined set. Percent-decoding yields raw bytes (matching the gem's `urlquery.decode` and Go's byte-oriented `url.Path`; an invalid-UTF-8 sequence like `%FF` is the raw byte, which OPA renders as U+FFFD only in JSON output).

## Structure

`builtins/uri/parser.rb` (driver), decomposed into `parser/escaping.rb` (percent engine) and `parser/host.rb` (authority/host/IPv6) to stay RubyCritic C-or-better; `uri.rb` is the thin handler. Public Parser API is `parse`/`hostname`/`port`; everything else is private. RBS in `sig/ruby/rego.rbs`.

## Compatibility verification

- 78-row golden spec table, all values pinned against `opa eval` 1.17.1.
- 4941-case fuzz oracle (gem vs `opa eval`): **0 parse / 0 is_valid mismatches**.
- 49-case binary-input (`base64.decode` -> ASCII-8BIT) parity sweep: **0 mismatches** (byte-level comparison).

## Review

Four-round adversarial panel (code-reviewer, architect, simplifier, security, spec-fidelity) to convergence. Fixed: a DoS crash on invalid-encoding input (uncaught `ArgumentError` aborting evaluation), an IPv6 empty-zone divergence (`[fe80::1%25]`), an over-strict encoding guard that rejected BINARY strings OPA parses (relaxed to `ascii_compatible? && valid_encoding?`), and an RBS public-API mismatch. R4: all five reviewers APPROVED.

Gates: rspec 1241/0 (3 pending) · rubocop 280/0 · reek 0 · steep clean · bundler-audit clean.

author: julien777z
body:
## What this is

A reusable, public GitHub Action that reviews pull requests with **Claude** or **Cursor** and posts severity-rated **inline comments** plus an **Approval Verdict** check run. Any repo can adopt it with `uses: julien777z/code-review-action@v1`.

```yaml
- uses: julien777z/code-review-action@v1
  with:
    anthropic-api-key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
    cursor-api-key: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
```

## Highlights

- **Backends.** `review-model: auto` (default) prefers Claude when an Anthropic key is set, else Cursor. `first-review-model` optionally uses a different backend for the opened/ready review.
- **Claude API or routine.** `claude-mode: api` (default) calls the Anthropic Messages API in CI with structured-output findings; `claude-mode: routine` fires a hosted routine, passing PR context, extra context, and policy in the fire payload. The routine id accepts `claude-routine-id` or `claude-routine-url` (mutually exclusive).
- **One pipeline.** Cursor and the Claude API produce findings that flow through a shared reconcile → verdict → post pipeline (thread dedup, stale-thread resolution, head re-gating, cancellation-safe check runs).
- **Tuning.** `additional-context`, `approval-include` / `approval-disable`, `min-severity`, `low-findings-cap`, `max-findings`, `include-paths` / `exclude-paths`, `trigger-phrase`, `review-drafts`, `author-associations`.
- **Bundled skill.** The code-review skill ships with the action (loaded at runtime), so consumers don't need it in their own repos.

## Layout

- `action.yml` — composite action; `src/code_review/` — engine (`config`, `github`, `review`, `prompt`, `models/{shared,claude,cursor}`, `review_backends/{cursor,claude}`, `runtime`).
- `.agents/` source-of-truth (skill + dev rules + settings) synced to `.claude` / `.cursor` / `.codex` by `agent-sync.yml`.
- `publish-release.yml` — manual version bump that tags `vX.Y.Z`, moves the `vX` major tag, and cuts a GitHub Release.

## Verification

- `pytest` — 87 tests passing (config, review engine, prompt, runtime selection/eligibility, backends).
- `agent_sync.py` runs and is idempotent (`--dry-run` reports no drift).
- All modules byte-compile; the entrypoint skips gracefully on ineligible events.

author: xcarter93
body:
This pull request introduces a unified file and image upload experience in the mobile app, significantly improving how users attach files and images across the project. It replaces direct usage of `expo-document-picker` with a new abstraction that supports picking from the photo library, camera, or files, and normalizes file handling and MIME type resolution. It also updates dependencies and permissions to support these features. **Unified File and Image Upload Experience** - Introduced a new utility, `pickUpload`, in `apps/mobile/lib/upload.ts` to allow users to choose between the photo library, camera, or files, normalizing the result and handling permissions and unsupported types. (`[apps/mobile/lib/upload.tsR1-R130](diffhunk://#diff-95d2b6bca5e371346238a28c181a1290162fe6ba345146619ea74cf1d5b84840R1-R130)`) - Added a MIME type resolver in `apps/mobile/lib/mime.ts` to ensure only supported file types are uploaded, improving reliability and error messaging for unsupported files. (`[apps/mobile/lib/mime.tsR1-R38](diffhunk://#diff-e94ee11ff17dd12b860935f14355e19f6676a5f159ee4aee7dfed0d9b32ba1cfR1-R38)`) - Updated `MentionInput` and `ProjectDocuments` components to use the new `pickUpload` utility and `expo-file-system` for native file uploads, replacing previous logic and removing custom MIME resolution code. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6acdd2778572acca6a2d8f933052548108c57fc9ccaf3b3ebae53d7e01bade5eL17-R18)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6acdd2778572acca6a2d8f933052548108c57fc9ccaf3b3ebae53d7e01bade5eL161-R189)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6acdd2778572acca6a2d8f933052548108c57fc9ccaf3b3ebae53d7e01bade5eL204-R224)`, `[[4]](diffhunk://#diff-4f2b4d9101548e681cea8a6f83df679cfb2927dde870f44c2a0c047afa87f9d9L15-R16)`, `[[5]](diffhunk://#diff-4f2b4d9101548e681cea8a6f83df679cfb2927dde870f44c2a0c047afa87f9d9L34-L64)`, `[[6]](diffhunk://#diff-4f2b4d9101548e681cea8a6f83df679cfb2927dde870f44c2a0c047afa87f9d9L99-R104)`) **Dependency and Permission Updates** - Added and configured `expo-image-picker` and `expo-file-system` dependencies, updated `app.json` to request appropriate permissions for photo and camera access, and updated lockfiles. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-45321158a63a427996bc608fa5ec52cb59ad7f4d1acf72902b9011f31b722799R99-R105)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-179bbaeea9e8295a4abee862073776f87f7dc3c78066c787b8fcdb8be71d5d83R6-R12)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-179bbaeea9e8295a4abee862073776f87f7dc3c78066c787b8fcdb8be71d5d83R40-R42)`, `[[4]](diffhunk://#diff-32824c984905bb02bc7ffcef96a77addd1f1602cff71a11fbbfdd7f53ee026bbR69-R77)`, `[[5]](diffhunk://#diff-32824c984905bb02bc7ffcef96a77addd1f1602cff71a11fbbfdd7f53ee026bbL6764-R6771)`, `[[6]](diffhunk://#diff-32824c984905bb02bc7ffcef96a77addd1f1602cff71a11fbbfdd7f53ee026bbR6790-R6799)`, `[[7]](diffhunk://#diff-32824c984905bb02bc7ffcef96a77addd1f1602cff71a11fbbfdd7f53ee026bbL18207-R18223)`) **Minor UI/UX Improvements** - Changed the email input placeholder in the organization creation flow to "Business email" for clarity. (`[apps/mobile/app/(onboarding)/create-organization.tsxL446-R449](diffhunk://#diff-82cb946c55b72f740069e72b6971af51e26d625ef9d315259c6f01fa6d6a182eL446-R449)`) - Improved the pre-filling of user identity fields (name and email) during onboarding, especially for Apple sign-ins. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-82cb946c55b72f740069e72b6971af51e26d625ef9d315259c6f01fa6d6a182eL81-R81)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-82cb946c55b72f740069e72b6971af51e26d625ef9d315259c6f01fa6d6a182eL113-R123)`) These changes collectively modernize and simplify file/image uploads, improve error handling, and enhance the user experience around attachments and onboarding.

Greptile Summary

This PR introduces a unified file/image upload abstraction for the mobile app, replacing direct `expo-document-picker` calls with a new `pickUpload` utility that lets users pick from the photo library, camera, or file browser. It also fixes the native upload path by using `FileSystem.uploadAsync` instead of a `fetch` blob (which fails in RN's bridgeless mode), and pre-fills the onboarding email field from Clerk for Apple sign-in users. - **New `pickUpload` utility** (`lib/upload.ts`, `lib/mime.ts`): presents a source-picker action sheet, requests permissions, normalizes results to a common `PickedFile` shape, and filters unsupported MIME types before returning. - **`MentionInput` and `ProjectDocuments` migrated** to `pickUpload` + `FileSystem.uploadAsync`; `ProjectDocuments` correctly guards against zero-size files before uploading, but `MentionInput` is missing that same guard. - **`package.json`** adds `expo-image-picker` and `expo-file-system` and sets `buildFromSource: [\".*\"]`, which forces every native package to compile from source on iOS — a broad pattern that will significantly inflate build times.

Confidence Score: 3/5

Safe to merge after fixing the zero-size attachment gap in MentionInput; the buildFromSource pattern should also be narrowed before shipping to CI. MentionInput allows attachments with an undetermined file size to proceed through the upload pipeline. The bytes reach Convex storage successfully, but the subsequent createMention call sends fileSize: 0, which the server is expected to reject — leaving orphaned storage objects and a silent failure for the user. ProjectDocuments handles this correctly, so the fix is a single guard line. Separately, building all native iOS packages from source will significantly slow down every subsequent build until that pattern is scoped down. apps/mobile/components/MentionInput.tsx (missing size guard) and apps/mobile/package.json (over-broad buildFromSource pattern).

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/mobile/lib/upload.ts | New upload abstraction that presents a source picker (Photo Library / Camera / Files), handles permissions, normalizes results into a common PickedFile shape, and filters unsupported MIME types. Logic is sound. | | apps/mobile/lib/mime.ts | Centralizes MIME resolution logic previously duplicated in ProjectDocuments. Correctly replaces the generic application/octet-stream fallback with an extension-based lookup; returns null for unknown types. | | apps/mobile/components/MentionInput.tsx | Replaces direct DocumentPicker/fetch usage with pickUpload + FileSystem.uploadAsync. Missing a guard for size === 0 after the disk-fallback, allowing zero-size files through to createMention where the server rejects fileSize <= 0. | | apps/mobile/components/ProjectDocuments.tsx | Correctly migrated to pickUpload + FileSystem.uploadAsync; properly guards against fileSize <= 0 before proceeding with the upload. | | apps/mobile/app/(onboarding)/create-organization.tsx | Renames nameSeeded → identitySeeded and adds email pre-filling from Clerk's primaryEmailAddress. The !email check prevents clobbering user input; logic is correct. | | apps/mobile/package.json | Adds expo-image-picker and expo-file-system dependencies. The buildFromSource: [".*"] autolinking config forces all native packages to compile from source on iOS, which is overly broad. | | apps/mobile/app.json | Adds expo-image-picker plugin config with appropriate user-facing permission strings for photo library and camera access. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A([User taps paperclip / Upload button]) --> B[pickUpload called] B --> C{chooseSource action sheet} C -->|Cancel| D([Return empty array]) C -->|Photo Library| E[requestMediaLibraryPermissionsAsync] C -->|Take Photo| F[requestCameraPermissionsAsync] C -->|Choose File| G[DocumentPicker.getDocumentAsync] E -->|denied| H([Alert + return empty]) F -->|denied| H E -->|granted| I[launchImageLibraryAsync] F -->|granted| J[launchCameraAsync] I --> K[normalizeImage + resolveMime] J --> K G --> L[resolveMime per asset] K -->|null

body:
## Task 6 — `review_sequence` config knob (customization-overlay)

Implements the review-gauntlet ordering as a four-layer config knob and rewires
`/execute-task`'s convergence phase to read it. Built on Task 3's four-layer
`config-get`.

- **Kickoff brief:** `specs/customization-overlay/kickoff-brief.md`
- **Task:** 6 (`tasks.md`)
- **REQs satisfied (Citations):** D-6 · REQ-C1.3, REQ-D1.3, REQ-E1.3, REQ-E1.4
- **Spec anchor (unchanged):** `69b89ff1f4119d9e5b08b79c7f1a6edd088c4e02`

### What changed
- **`scripts/resolve-review-sequence.sh`** (new) — resolves `review_sequence`
  *through* `config-get` (REQ-D1.1; no layer logic re-implemented), parses the
  inline list, validates each name against the nestable-review-skill predicate
  (a skill whose `SKILL.md` `argument-hint` declares `--nested` — exactly
  REQ-D1.3's definition; today `{polish, self-review}`), and applies the
  REQ-E1.4 by-layer malformed policy. Prints the validated ordered names, one
  per line.
- **`config/defaults.yml`** — `review_sequence: [polish]`. The default
  reproduces today's single `/polish --nested` convergence, so out-of-the-box
  behavior is unchanged (default-preserving).
- **`docs/options-reference.md`** — documents the option (`check-options-reference.sh` passes).
- **`skills/execute-task/SKILL.md`** — convergence phase rewired to resolve the
  knob and run each named skill in order with `--nested`; description +
  invariant generalized from hardcoded `/polish` to the gauntlet.

### Malformed-by-layer policy (REQ-D1.3 → REQ-E1.4)
A `review_sequence` value naming an unknown or non-nestable skill, or an empty
list, is malformed. By the layer that supplied the winning value:
- **repo-tracked:** hard-fail (exit 4) — a broken shared gauntlet never
  silently degrades a team (also propagates `config-get`'s exit 4 for a
  structurally malformed repo-tracked file).
- **adopter / machine-local:** warn on stderr and degrade to the core default.

### Tests added (`tests/test-resolve-review-sequence.sh`, 18 cases)
Resolution across all four layers (last-layer-wins), ordering preserved
verbatim (not sorted), bare-scalar + inline-list parse, whitespace/comment
tolerance, the by-layer policy (degrade+warn vs exit-4 hard-fail), a
structurally malformed repo-tracked file, a **characterization test locking the
documented degrade-to-core behavior**, the **newline-terminated output
contract**, the **usage guard (exit 2)**, and the **absent-in-every-layer
fallback**. `mise run check` (full CI) green.

### Manual verification — REQ-D1.3 ordering scenario (`[manual]`, R7)
Verified end-to-end against the **real** `skills/` root and recorded in the
brief's risk register (§7): default→`polish`; adopter `[self-review, polish]`→in
order; repo-tracked reverse→order preserved + wins (last-layer-wins);
machine-local bad-name→degrade+warn; repo-tracked bad-name→exit 4. R7 discharged.

### Polish convergence (execute-task audit record)
Solo repo; active kickoff brief. Loop converged (self-critique re-pass produced
no new findings).

| Bucket | Items |
| --- | --- |
| Auto-applicable | none (tool-grounded checks — shellcheck, shfmt, yamllint, markdownlint, check-options-reference — were already green) |
| Agent-resolvable | 1 — characterization test locking the degrade-to-core contract (commit `51f695d`); evidence: passes after, full `mise run check` green, aligned with the brief's degrade+warn policy |
| Needs sign-off | none |
| Needs human judgment | none unresolvable |

**Pending-sign-off checklist:** superseded — see the regenerated canonical
checklist under *Self-review pass* below (now carries **PS-1**). **Declined log
at polish convergence:** none.

### Implementation notes (decisions beyond the brief's assumptions)
- **Degrade target is the core default, not a strict per-layer cascade.** When a
  bad name comes from adopter/machine-local, the resolver degrades to the core
  default (always-valid, behavior-preserving) rather than honoring an
  intermediate valid lower overlay. Reason: `config-get` exposes only the merged
  winning value (`--explain`), not per-layer values, and REQ-D1.1 forbids a
  skill from re-reading layers itself. This satisfies REQ-E1.4's degrade+warn
  and is the true next-lower layer in the dominant single-overlay case.
  Documented in the script header, locked by a test, and logged as a
  future-refinement observation.
- **"Nestable review skill" predicate** = `argument-hint` declares `--nested`
  (REQ-D1.3's own definition), discovered from `skills/` so it self-maintains.

### Coordination note (not a blocker for this draft)
This branch forked at `f859ef8`; `origin/main` has since advanced (Task 5 #40,
spec-walkthrough #44). Main also touched `skills/execute-task/SKILL.md` (a
*different* section — decision-domains wiring), `tasks.md` (Task 5's block), and
the brief. A **main-merge + conflict resolution is needed before the
draft→ready flip** (worker-owned resolution per the coordination protocol;
typically orchestrator-directed). The observations-log append will be a
trivial keep-both conflict.

---

### Self-review pass (audit record, standalone, 2026-06-17)

Gate-wired single pass over `origin/main...HEAD`. Discovery fanned out one
read-only sub-agent per lens (diff is a 244-line security-relevant parser + a
240-line test + doc/spec edits). Full `mise run check` green before and after.

author: ellingtonsp
body:
## Root cause
Every scheduled Uptime/Response Time/Graphs/Summary/Static Site run was crashing on Node 24 (GitHub's runner migration) because `upptime/uptime-monitor@v1.38.0` bundles a `node-libcurl` native binary built for Node 20's ABI (`NODE_MODULE_VERSION 115` vs Node 24's `137`). Result: a GitHub workflow-failure email every ~5–45 min. **The monitored sites were never down** (no open incidents; prod + staging independently verified `200 ok`).

## Fix
Bump all 5 workflows `v1.38.0` → **`v1.42.6`** (current latest), which ships a Node 24-compatible binary.

## Verification
Triggered `Uptime CI` via `workflow_dispatch` on this branch → **success** on Node 24. Remaining annotations are non-fatal (the cosmetic `'token'` input warning, present before too, and the `actions/checkout@v4` deprecation notice).

body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
>
> 1. Make sure you have read our [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
> 1. Ensure there is an associated issue and you have been assigned to it
> 1. Use the correct syntax to link this PR: `Fixes #<issue number>`.

## Summary

Five bulk-deletion methods in the workflow repositories return or
accumulate `CursorResult.rowcount` directly. SQLAlchemy/DBAPI drivers
can legitimately return `None` from `rowcount`, causing
`TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +=: 'int' and 'NoneType'`
in batched loops or violating the `-> int` return contract elsewhere.

Sibling methods in the same files already use the defensive pattern
`result.rowcount or 0` (e.g. `sqlalchemy_api_workflow_run_repository.py`
lines 521, 570, 581, 583, 588, 620, 631, 633, 638). This change applies
the same coercion to the five missing sites:

- `delete_expired_executions` (node-execution)
- `delete_executions_by_app` (node-execution)
- `delete_executions_by_ids` (node-execution)
- `delete_runs_by_ids` (workflow-run)
- `delete_runs_by_app` (workflow-run)

author: omninetopensource
body:
💡 **What:** 
Optimized `src/features/sidebar/store/useConversationsStore.ts` by removing several redundant array allocations in the state management functions. 
Specifically:
1. Changed `splitAndSortConversations` to accept `Iterable<Conversation>` instead of an array, allowing `mergeConversations` to pass `map.values()` directly and avoiding an `Array.from()` call.
2. Removed redundant shallow copies `[...conversations]` before calling `.sort()` in `sortByPinnedAt` and `sortByUpdatedAt`, since `splitAndSortConversations` already constructs fresh arrays before calling them.
3. Changed `updateConversationTitle` to use chained `.find()` searches (`pinned.find() ?? normal.find()`) instead of creating a new merged array with the spread operator `[...pinned, ...normal]`.

🎯 **Why:** 
The conversation store state manipulations (especially `mergeConversations` and `updateConversationTitle`) run frequently when new conversations are loaded, updated, or when their metadata changes. Unnecessary O(N) array allocations—like `Array.from()` to convert a Map to an array, shallow copies before sorting newly-minted arrays, and array concatenation via spread operators just to `.find()` an item—increase garbage collection pressure and create measurable CPU overhead, particularly for users with large conversation histories.

📊 **Impact:** 
Eliminates at least three O(N) memory allocations per state merge operation and eliminates one O(N) allocation per title update operation. Searching operations in `updateConversationTitle` avoid iterating through the entire list if the item is found early in the `pinnedConversations` list. Expected to noticeably reduce memory pressure and improve execution speed for large datasets.

🔬 **Measurement:** 
Run `pnpm check` and `pnpm lint` to ensure static types properly track the shift from `Array` to `Iterable` and that no syntax errors were introduced. Open the application, perform actions like pinning, unpinning, and renaming conversations to visually verify that sorting and state persistence continue to behave perfectly while generating fewer allocations in browser memory profilers.

author: terkelg
body:
Major **2.0** rewrite to modern ESM + TypeScript, native tooling, and a refreshed CI/release pipeline. Runtime behaviour of the escape codes is unchanged — this is purely a packaging/modernization release.

Closes #12.

> [!WARNING]
> **Breaking:** the package is now **ESM-only** and requires **Node.js >= 20** at runtime. CommonJS consumers and older Node should stay on the `1.x` line. (Contributing requires Node.js >= 22, since the test suite runs the TypeScript source directly via type stripping.)

## What changed

- **Source → TypeScript.** `src/index.js` → `src/index.ts` with inline types. The diff against 1.x is only the unavoidable bits: drop `'use strict'`, add type annotations, and `module.exports` → `export`.
- **Named exports only.** `import { cursor } from 'sisteransi'` or `import * as ansi from 'sisteransi'`. No default export (1.x had none either), which keeps the cleanest `require(esm)` shape and generated `.d.ts`.
- **Build with `tsc`.** Ships compiled `dist/index.js` + auto-generated `dist/index.d.ts` (replacing the hand-maintained `.d.ts`), wired up via a modern `exports` map and `"type": "module"`. Minimal `tsconfig.json` (target, module, declaration, outDir, strict).
- **Runtime floor `>= 20`.** Because consumers import the compiled JS (not the TS source), they don't need Node 22's type stripping — that's a dev-only requirement. `engines.node` is set to `>=20` to match the runnable output.
- **Native test runner.** Dropped `tape`/`tap-spec` for `node:test` + `node:assert/strict` (`test/index.ts`), run directly against the TS source via Node's native type-stripping — no build step needed for `npm test`.
- **CI refresh.** GitHub Actions with `actions/checkout@v6` + `actions/setup-node@v6` and least-privilege `permissions: contents: read`. A `test` job runs the suite on Node **22 & 24**; a `dist` job builds and imports `dist/` on Node **20** to verify the declared runtime floor. Committed `package-lock.json` + `npm ci`. Removed `.travis.yml` and the nyc/codecov coverage step.
- **Trusted publishing (refs #13).** New `release.yml` publishes to npm on a GitHub Release via **trusted publishing / OIDC** (`id-token: write`, no `NPM_TOKEN`), refreshing npm to the `>= 11.5.1` required for it. Provenance is generated automatically.
- **Docs & housekeeping.** Readme + example updated to ESM (and fixed a pre-existing `process.stdin.write` → `process.stdout.write` bug in the example). `typescript` is now the only devDependency.

## Migration (1.x → 2.0)

```js
// before (1.x, CommonJS)
const { cursor } = require('sisteransi');
const ansi = require('sisteransi');

// after (2.0, ESM)
import { cursor } from 'sisteransi';
import * as ansi from 'sisteransi';
```

## Verification

- `npm run build` emits `dist/` with full `.d.ts` declarations
- `npm test` — all 5 suites pass on Node 22.22
- CI green: `test` on Node 22 & 24, `dist` smoke import on Node 20

body:
## PR 1 — D-005 · Mayor · Reabierto — Alta de producto no persiste

**Síntoma:** el gerente completa el formulario, toca "AGREGAR PRESENTACIÓN" → "CREAR PRODUCTO", la app regresa al catálogo **sin toast** y el producto no aparece.

### Causa raíz (nueva, distinta del feedback de #17)
`PresentacionForm` renderizaba un **`<form>` anidado dentro del `<form>` de `ProductoForm`** (el form del producto envuelve toda la pantalla, incluida la presentación inline). Con forms anidados, el `submit` del botón **"Agregar presentación"** burbujea y dispara **también** el `onSubmit` del form externo (`ProductoForm.handleSubmit`) — pero con el estado `presentaciones` **aún sin actualizar** (el `setState` de añadir la presentación no ha vaciado todavía). Resultado: un guardado prematuro e inconsistente del producto, sin la presentación adjunta, antes de que el flujo llegue al toast esperado.

Por eso el toast de éxito/error de #17 "nunca dispara": el submit que se ejecuta no es el que el usuario cree.

### Correcciones
1. **Eliminado el form anidado** — `PresentacionForm` ya no usa `<form>`/`type="submit"`: es un `<div>` con botón `type="button"` que llama al handler directamente. Sin forms anidados no hay doble submit ni estado intermedio; **"Crear producto" es el único submit** de la pantalla.
2. **Orden de operaciones explícito** (y ya correcto): se crea `PRODUCTO_BASE` primero, luego `PRESENTACION` con su `producto_base_id`. El toast de éxito sólo dispara **tras confirmar ambos inserts**.
3. **Logging explícito** del error en el `catch` (`console.error`) para diagnosticar la causa raíz, y mensaje al usuario con el detalle cuando existe.

> Nota sobre validación de BD: la app es offline-first — el insert local es la fuente de la lista del catálogo, y los errores de servidor (RLS/constraint) se reflejan vía el `SyncStatusBadge`. La RLS de gerente sobre `producto_base`/`presentacion` ya es correcta (`*_gerente_insert` con `es_gerente()`).

### Verificación
- `tsc` + `vite build` limpio.
- `eslint` limpio.
- **156 tests en verde** (155 base + `CAT-106`: alta de "Trapeador Microseda 1pz" + presentación → ambos quedan indexados como activos, la misma consulta `where activo=1` que usa la lista del catálogo).
- Sin romper casos de `docs/trazabilidad-qa-fase5.md`.

Verificación manual esperada: dar de alta "Trapeador Microseda 1pz" (unidad pieza, factor 1, $45/$65) → toast visible → producto aparece en el catálogo sin navegación adicional.

**Título:** `fix(catalogo): producto alta — fix silent insert failure and toast trigger`

author: jhurliman
body:
## The bug — self-host can't bootstrap its schema
The only schema migration, `SelfHost`, **assumes a pre-existing multi-tenant SaaS schema** and *alters* it (`ALTER TABLE "users" ADD COLUMN …`, references long-dropped columns like `gitlab_id`/`stripe_*`). But a self-hosted install always starts from an **empty** database, so on a fresh DB it fails immediately:
```
relation "users" does not exist
```
i.e. fresh self-hosting can't create its schema at all. (Found while standing up a self-hosted instance.)

## Fix
- **Delete `1717000000000-SelfHost.ts`** — no self-hoster has the SaaS schema it transforms.
- **Add `1700000000000-InitialSchema.ts`** — creates the full self-host schema **from scratch** (the exact shape the current entities produce via `synchronize`; generated by dumping a synchronized schema). Statements run individually since TypeORM's query runner uses the single-statement protocol.
- **`task_queue` NOTIFY trigger** — an `AFTER INSERT` trigger `pg_notify`s the worker so it wakes **immediately** on enqueue from any source, instead of waiting for its ~10s poll. Drops the now-redundant app-level `NOTIFY` in `upload.ts`.
- `EnsureCascadeDeletes` is unchanged and still runs after the baseline (idempotent).

## Verified
Ran `InitialSchema` → `EnsureCascadeDeletes` through the **actual TypeORM migration runner** on a fresh Postgres: 7 tables + the trigger created, both recorded in `migrations`. `build:all` / `lint:all` / `test:all` (api 69 against real Postgres, worker 101) green.

> Note: this changes the migration baseline. Since no self-hoster has the old SaaS schema, fresh installs are the only consumers; existing prod (if any) is on its own established schema and unaffected by the new baseline name (it won't re-run table creation).

author: gh123man
body:
## Summary

Fixes onboard profiles created or renamed by OpenSnek appearing broken in Synapse even though they still work on the mouse.

The root cause appears to be the metadata owner field: Synapse-created profiles use a 64-character hex owner hash, while OpenSnek was writing the short `OpenSnek` marker. The mouse accepts that marker, but Synapse rejects the profile in its UI.

## Changes

- Default onboard profile metadata to a Synapse-compatible 64-character owner hash.
- Preserve an existing Synapse owner hash from the target profile or another assigned profile when writing USB/Bluetooth profile metadata.
- Treat metadata reads as complete only when UUID, name, and owner hash are present.
- Add `OpenSnekProbe usb-profile-clone` for guarded USB profile metadata/content repair with strict readback.
- Document the owner-hash requirement and update focused tests.

## Validation

- `swift build --package-path OpenSnek --product OpenSnekProbe`
- `swift test --package-path OpenSnek --filter BridgeClientUSBWriteSemanticsTests`
- `swift test --package-path OpenSnek --filter BridgeClientBluetoothFallbackTests/testCompleteBluetoothOnboardProfileMetadataRequiresAllIdentityFields`

author: zorlin
body:
Part of #8. Removes the crate-wide `#![allow(clippy::all)]` and runs `cargo clippy --fix`.

**Why:** Jetpack (formerly jetporch) was abandoned ~5 years ago with an idiosyncratic "house style" (pervasive explicit `return`s, needless borrows, etc.). As a revival, we're modernizing to current idiomatic Rust rather than preserving the old style — Rust has converged on these idioms.

**What:** ~1,240 of ~1,430 lints auto-fixed — implicit returns, needless borrows removed, redundant field names collapsed, collapsible `if`s, etc. 79 files, net −123 lines.

**Verification:** build clean (zero warnings), all tests pass, `cargo fmt --check` clean.

**Remaining:** ~194 non-auto-fixable lints (`ptr_arg` `&String`→`&str`, `unnecessary_unwrap`, a few `too_many_arguments`/`module_inception`) — these need manual handling and will land in a follow-up. CI's clippy job uses `-W` (warn), so this is green as-is.

author: heyarnoldo
body:
## Qué

Habilita el **offline desde arranque en frío** en desktop. El Electron ya **no carga la web remota** (que sin internet fallaba); ahora **empaqueta la web** y la sirve local vía un protocolo `app://` con fallback SPA, así la app **siempre abre**. Solo el **API URL** se configura por tenant, en runtime.

Es la **base (PR A)** del plan offline. Las piezas B (cachear catálogo) y C (PIN global + login offline) vienen después y dependen de esto.

## Cambios

- **main.ts**: protocolo `app://` sirviendo `dist-electron/web` con fallback a index.html (mantiene BrowserRouter); config guarda `apiUrl` (no `webUrl`); el setup pide la URL del API; IPC sync `get-api-url`; CSP permite `app://` + https/wss.
- **preload.ts**: expone `electronAPI.apiUrl` (leído sincrónicamente).
- **web**: el cliente api y conectividad resuelven la base desde `electronAPI.apiUrl` primero, luego `VITE_API_URL` (el deploy web NO se afecta).
- **build**: copia `apps/web/dist` → `dist-electron/web` antes de electron-builder.

## Verificación

CI compila todo (Electron + web + 69 tests). **El runtime de Electron NO es verificable en CI** — hay que **construir el instalador (`pnpm --filter @app/desktop dist:win`) y correrlo** para validar carga local + offline.

## Salvedad importante (auth)

El login **online** desde el origen `app://` hacia el API `https://` es cross-site. Puede requerir **COOKIE_SAMESITE=none** y agregar el origen `app://` al CORS del API para que la cookie de sesión viaje. A validar al probar el instalador.
EOF

## Summary
Wave 4 (final remediation wave) — 19 low/medium-severity defects across browser, sandbox, channels, MCP transports, observability, TUI, and cross-platform tools. From `.planning/2026-06-18-DEEP-SWEEP-AUDIT.md`.

### Browser lifecycle / policy
- **F17** Browserbase dropped `BrowserPolicy` (redirect-SSRF unenforceable cloud-side) → refused under restrictive policy, falls back to Camoufox.
- **F18** Camoufox `final_url` SSRF check failed **open** when absent → now fails closed.
- **F23** healthcheck task held `Arc<Self>` (cycle defeating Drop) → `Weak`. **F24** double `start_reaper` leaked tasks → cancel prior. **F25** SIGTERM on a reusable raw PID → stashed `Child`. **F38** `ensure_session` race orphaned sessions → re-check + close loser.

### Sandbox / channels / transport leaks
- **F4** bwrap + sandbox-exec leaked the process tree on timeout → `kill_on_drop(true)`.
- **F9** unbounded `VecDeque` inbox across **10** channel adapters → one shared bounded helper in `wcore-channels` (cap 1024, drop-oldest + warn).
- **F26** MCP SSE `close()` left parked requests waiting the full timeout → drain + closed flag. **F33** MCP stdio `close()` only detached the reader → `handle.abort()`. **F42** `InMemorySink` poison hid traces → `into_inner()`.

### TUI / cross-platform tools
- **F21** CredentialsModal falsely claimed live `.env` apply + no-op rebind → honest text, rebind removed. **F22** `/mcp add` dropped `${cred:}` errors → surfaced. **F37** out-of-order deferred rebinds → generation counter. **F40** `/doctor` re-probe leaked threads → guarded.
- **F34** Windows stdio metachar program names through `cmd /C` → quote on metachar. **F35** findstr leading-`/` pattern as switch → `/R /C:`. **F36** grep root fell to process cwd → contained to jail. **F43** grep `Command::new` → `shell_command_argv`.

body:
## Summary

Adds a small **provider seam** — `roboco/llm/providers/` — so the orchestrator can drive agent backends beyond Claude Code, and lands the first non-Claude backend: **`GrokProvider`** for xAI's `grok-build-0.1`.

This is the seam to review/co-implement for the xAI integration. It's intentionally a **draft**: the abstraction, routing, key handling, migrations and tests are complete and green, while the dedicated Grok agent image + the exact OpenAI-protocol CLI invocation are the remaining piece to finalise together with xAI.

## What's here

- **`AgentProvider` ABC + `ProviderRegistry`** (`base.py`, `registry.py`) keyed by `ModelProvider`.
- **`GrokProvider`** (`grok.py`) — xAI is OpenAI-compatible *only* (no Anthropic-Messages endpoint), so a Grok agent runs an OpenAI-protocol runtime pointed at `https://api.x.ai/v1` instead of the `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` injection the other providers use. Crucially it **reuses the orchestrator's existing mount/auth assembly**, so a Grok agent inherits the **same MCP gateway + tool-manifest wiring** (`roboco-flow` / `roboco-do`) as every other agent *by construction* — it cannot spawn gateway-blind. The xAI endpoint is injected as `OPENAI_*` (the provider routing fields are blanked before the shared mount step so it's never mislabelled `ANTHROPIC_*`), and the prompt is passed via **env, never an argv positional**, which structurally avoids CLI flag-injection.
- **`ClaudeCodeProvider`** (`claude_code.py`) — reference adapter over the current Claude Code spawn.
- **Purely additive routing**: a guard at the top of `_spawn_container` delegates only when a dedicated provider is registered (today just `GROK`). Anthropic / Ollama Cloud / self-hosted spawns run the existing path **byte-for-byte unchanged**.
- **`ModelProvider.GROK`** (migration `038`) + a **seeded Grok provider row** (migration `039`) + a `grok-build-0.1` **catalog entry** so an agent/role/global can be routed to Grok.
- **`GET/PUT /api/providers/grok-key`** — store the xAI key (Fernet-encrypted, reusing the existing provider-key machinery).
- **Tests** (`tests/unit/llm/test_providers.py`, `tests/unit/runtime/test_provider_routing.py`): registry behaviour; GrokProvider gateway wiring, no `ANTHROPIC_*` leak, prompt-injection safety, default base_url, failure paths; ClaudeCodeProvider delegation; and the additive routing.

## Status

- `ruff format --check .` ✅ · `ruff check .` ✅ · `mypy roboco/ tests/` ✅ · 803 unit tests pass (incl. enum-migration parity for `038`/`039`). No `# type: ignore` / `# noqa`.

## Deliberate follow-ups (not in this draft)

- The **`roboco-agent-grok` image** + exact OpenAI-protocol CLI/MCP invocation (the entrypoint consumes the env contract `GrokProvider` sets) — the piece to build/test with xAI.
- A **panel Grok key card** (the `/grok-key` API is ready; mirrors the Ollama card).
- **Cost accounting** for Grok in `roboco/billing/pricing.py` (xAI is paid; currently treated as `$0` like local — needs xAI's token rates).

## Credit

The provider-abstraction direction (`AgentProvider` ABC + registry) was introduced by @gogosoto in #170; this lands a slimmed version of that abstraction on current `master` and defers #170's broader orchestrator decomposition to its own refactor.

author: mavaali
body:
## Summary

Stage 2 of the cortex consolidation loop (Component A) — birth mode, revision mode, shadow-mode edge writes, the axis-decorrelation report, and a from-scratch rework that makes `derives_from` **edge direction reliable**. Runs `shadow_mode` + `ratify:false` by default, so merging turns nothing on (the loop proposes; humans ratify).

Builds on Stage 1 (the scheduler, already on `main`). `main` is an ancestor — clean merge.

### What's here
- **Birth mode** — unprocessed doc → top-K neighbors → foundational-ordering direction elicitation (temp 0) → seeds k=0 candidate edges; full top-K + verdicts logged to the birth trace for recall@K.
- **Revision mode** — panel of M votes on a due edge, **majority-decides-once**: majority-survives → observe each surviving vote with a distinct store axis (k accrues); majority-fails → one contest; tie → surface.
- **Shadow mode** — `makeObserve`/`makeContest` factories route edge writes to `shadow-actions.jsonl` (calibration) with `edges.jsonl` untouched; blast/impact/budget math per the §11.5 brief.
- **`derives_from` direction** — foundational-ordering `{related, premise}` elicitation (replaces the broken derives/depends token), neighbor-content loading, **both-orders reconciliation** (order-disagreement → symmetric/pending), and symmetric edges as direction-unconfirmed pending edges that don't propagate triggers. Edge keys are **canonical** so a post-edit flip collapses to symmetric instead of forking a twin.
- **Decorrelation report** — reuses the shared foundational prompt (both orders), accuracy-gated.
- CLI: `daftari consolidate --mode scan|birth|revision|both`, `--report decorrelation --fixture`, `--budget`/`--max-births`/`--max-panels`/`--model`; exit-code hierarchy 0/2/3/4/5/6/7.

### Validation
- **Real-prose direction gate**: 96–100% accuracy, perfect order-consistency on curated clear-direction pairs (failed first on ambiguous `draft_novel` pairs → re-curated; symmetric emission 80–100%).
- **Formal decorrelation re-run** on the contamination-free v2 fixture (39 edges): **97.4% PASS** (both-orders) — a decisive reversal of the old token runs (−15.69pp lift).
- **Two adversarial review passes** (3 reviewers each): direction rework, then the pre-direction Stage 2 surface. Every confirmed finding fixed — incl. two CRITICAL revision-mode bugs (panel never accrued k; no vote aggregation), the flipped-directed twin, a stale-baseline silent-skip (now exit 7), and a birth-trace-loss state bug.
- **1125 pass / 3 skip**, `tsc` + `biome` clean.

### Known characteristics / follow-ups
- **Cost**: option-c doubles the per-neighbor direction calls (both orders). Bounded by `--max-births`/`--budget`; the cost estimate reflects it. Shadow mode = no real writes.
- **Deferred (graduation gate, not this PR)**: the option-c stuck-pending / false-symmetric rate on the *uncurated ambiguous tail* must be measured in shadow against a real vault before turning shadow **off**. Tracked in `docs/superpowers/drafts/2026-06-16-stage2-decorrelation-verdict.md` ("Ongoing (shadow)").
- v6 schema bump rebuilds the ephemeral index automatically on open. No release/publish in this PR.

- [ ] `npm test` — 1125 pass / 3 skip
- [ ] `npm run lint` (biome) — clean
- [ ] Optional: `daftari consolidate --report decorrelation --fixture tests/fixtures/decorrelation-fixture-v2.json` (needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`)
