## Vague 3 — PR 1 : la primitive « référence de loyer marché » (sans le wiring matching)

Signal **backend déterministe (0 LLM)** qui mesure la **position d'un loyer demandé vs le marché** de son segment. Cette PR pose la primitive seule : **aucun impact matching** (le wiring arrive en PR2), donc mergeable indépendamment.

Plan maître : `docs/estimation-loyer-plan.md` (#672). Spec : `docs/estimation-loyer-vague2-concevoir.md` (incluse ici).

### Contenu
- **MV `public.market_rent_stats`** — comparables loyer/m² (`COALESCE(current_price,price)/surface_m2`, calculé live, jamais la colonne `price_per_m2` qui est 75 % NULL sur le rent) par segment `canton×type×bande-surface`, avec raffinement `ville`/`NPA` là où `n≥20`, winsorisée p2.5/p97.5. Refresh `CONCURRENTLY` post `flatfox-sync` (cron `45 4`).
- **Module pur** `supabase/functions/_shared/rent-reference.ts` — `surfaceBand`, `buildRentStatsIndex`, `rentPosition` (fallback `NPA→ville→canton`, `n≥20`), courbe `position→frac` (hump borné, neutre 0.5 au marché), `buildRentReasonSuffix`. **19/19 tests unit**.
- `app_config.market_rent_reference_v1` (barème tunable) + RPC `get_market_rent_reference_config()`.

### Vérification
- **Migration appliquée en prod à la main via Supabase MCP** (verrou billing GitHub Actions), idempotente. MV live : **285 segments** (83 canton + 80 ville + 122 NPA), `min n_comparables = 20`, `REFRESH … CONCURRENTLY` OK.
- `npm run build` vert ; `vitest` 19/19.
- **Bug attrapé en vérif live** (raté par la revue 3-lentilles) : `REFRESH … CONCURRENTLY` exige un index unique **colonne-pure** (ni expression, ni partiel) ; l'index sur `COALESCE(...)` est un index d'expression et était rejeté → clé matérialisée en colonne `seg_key`. Sans ça le cron nocturne aurait échoué en silence.

### Notes
- Le code edge (`rent-reference.ts`) **n'est pas consommé** tant que PR2 (wiring) n'est pas livrée → zéro changement de comportement matching.
- CI possiblement bloquée par le verrou billing GitHub Actions ; merge sur la base de la vérif locale + live.

body:
## Summary

V2 gating for the follow-up and first-message paths, plus a debug aid for tracing `leads_status_id` mutations.

### V2 follow-up engagement (`FollowUpEngagementCommand` + `FollowUpEngagementAction`)
- Skip + log when v2 is enabled (`intelligence_lead_type_mode_v2` on company) and `ai_follow_up` lead setting is NOT `true` / `1`. Tracked via `DailyReportService` (`ai_follow_up_engagement_skip_reason_ai_follow_up_not_enabled`) and persisted on the `FollowUpLog` metadata.
- Defense in depth: `FollowUpEngagementAction` constructor throws `FollowUpException` if the same guard would skip — protects callers that bypass the command.
- In v2, `ai_mode` (FULL_ON / SUPPORT / IDLE) no longer gates follow-up; only `ai_follow_up` does. `$muteAiAgent` collapses to `false` when v2 is on. V1 behavior unchanged.

### V2 first-message outreach (`LeadAgentFirstMessageOutreachActivity`)
- In v2: only send when lead type's `first_fu_active_default` is exactly `1` / `true` AND `$lead->hasBeenContacted()` is false. Otherwise `$disableSending = true` (same path as the legacy disable) and `v2_skip_reason` is added to the workflow return so we can see which side failed.
- Three skip reasons: `first_fu_active_default_not_one`, `already_contacted`, `first_fu_active_default_not_one_and_already_contacted`.
- V1 behavior unchanged.

### New helpers (`LeadConfigurationService`)
- `isAiFollowUpEnabled(Lead $lead): bool` — strict (`true`, `1`, `'1'`, `'true'`).
- `isFirstFollowUpActiveDefault(Lead $lead): bool` — strict against `$leadType->config[first_fu_active_default_key]`.

### Debug aid (`LeadObserver::updating`)
- On every `leads_status_id` dirty, writes a **private + locked** system message into the lead's `systemNotes` channel with status from/to + truncated PHP call stack. Helps trace which path is mutating the status. Marked `// DEBUG` and isolated in `writeStatusChangeDebugNote()` — easy to remove. Wrapped in `try/catch Throwable` so it never blocks the Lead update.

## Test plan
- [ ] Lead in app with `intelligence_lead_type_mode_v2 = true` and `ai_follow_up = 1`: follow-up runs.
- [ ] Same lead with `ai_follow_up = false` / `null`: command skips with `ai_follow_up_not_enabled`; direct action call throws `FollowUpException`.
- [ ] Lead with `ai_mode = IDLE` in v2 company: no longer skipped by `mute_ai_agent` (only `ai_follow_up` decides).
- [ ] Lead in v1 company: behavior identical to before (regression check).
- [ ] First-message outreach in v2: `first_fu_active_default = 1` + not contacted → sends; either `false` or `hasBeenContacted = true` → `disableSending` + `v2_skip_reason` populated.
- [ ] Trigger any path that mutates `leads_status_id` (UI update, close-sold workflow) → private locked note appears in lead's system thread with the call stack.

author: propensive
body:
Abacist's `Quanta` now takes its base (smallest) unit as its type parameter and carries the coarser divisions in a `Form` type member, so two quantities measured in the same base unit but divided differently — hours-minutes-seconds and minutes-seconds, say — share the common supertype `Quanta[Seconds[1]]` and can be compared with one another.

A `Quanta` type is now written with the base unit as the parameter and the divisions after `in`:

```scala
type Hms = Quanta[Seconds[1]] in (Minutes[1], Hours[1])
type Ms  = Quanta[Seconds[1]] in (Minutes[1])
```

Both are subtypes of `Quanta[Seconds[1]]`, so differently-divided values can be held together and compared:

```scala
val a: Hms = Quanta(1, 2, 3)
val b: Ms  = Quanta(4, 5)
val times: List[Quanta[Seconds[1]]] = List(a, b)
a > b   // compared by their common base unit
```

Values are constructed with `Quanta(…)`, inferring the base and divisions from the expected type; where there is no expected type, ascribe it — `(Quanta(3, 2): Weight).show`. The base unit is bounded `<: Units[?, ?]` and the divisions `<: Tuple | Units[?, ?]`, so non-unit `Quanta` types are rejected at compile time.

author: pekkah
body:
Closes #290. Follow-up to #209 (work item #4).

## Problem
`BatchVerify` set `gdnSnapRing=true`, forcing `GdnBlockBatched` into the per-position View loop (k×8 launches/layer via `GdnRecurrenceDecode`) **plus** ~2×(k−1)×numGdn `CopyDeviceRegion` launches (≈96×(k−1) on the 27B-MTP) — just to snapshot each token's GDN `(scan, conv)` state into the rollback ring, instead of the #114-B fused `GdnRecurrenceScan` path the prefill trunk uses.

## Change
Keep the fused path for verify and capture the state **during** the scan:

1. **`llm_gdn_recurrence_scan`** — optional `ring_scan`/`ring_slot_stride`/`n_capture`. In Pass B, where each thread already writes the post-update `state[off] = sij`, it also mirrors `sij` into ring slot `i` for `i < n_capture`. **Zero extra launches**; the scan arithmetic and the live-state evolution stay byte-unchanged (the ring is a disjoint `__restrict__` buffer).
2. **New `llm_gdn_conv1d_state_capture_ring`** — one launch writes every ring slot's conv state (slot `i` = `state_update` with `nTok = i+1`), run **before** the in-place conv state advance so it reads the pre-batch state.
3. **Flat ring** — the snapshot ring is now two contiguous tensors `[slots × numGdn × perLayerFloats]` so the kernels can stride across slots; OOM degrades by retrying fewer slots. `Capture/RestoreGdnRingSlot` re-point to the flat buffer (still used by the `SHARPI_BATCHED_GDN_SCAN=0` fallback + all restores).

Verify always uses the byte-exact scan (never the opt-in chunked-prefill form), so it stays in the same precision class as prefill/`Forward` — **bit-identity holds by composition** over the already-proven #114-B fused path. Rollback correctness is preserved (`RestoreBatchSnapshot` reads slot `lengthAfter − startPos − 1`).

## Tests
- New model-free bit-exactness oracles: `GdnRecurrenceScan_RingCapture_BitwiseMatchesPerSlotState`, `GdnConv1dStateCaptureRing_BitwiseMatchesPerSlotUpdate` (multi-layer ring, non-zero target layer; asserts capture doesn't perturb the scan and that untouched layers stay zero).
- All 10 `CudaGdnBatchedTrunkTests` pass.
- All 3 `CudaMtpBatchVerifyTests` (27B-MTP parity / junk-draft rollback / e2e decode) pass in **both** default and `SHARPI_BATCHED_GDN_SCAN=0` modes.
- Build clean (0 warnings, TreatWarningsAsErrors).

## Perf (RTX 4070 Ti, Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-Q4_K_M, `-g -1`, temp 0)
Warm A/B with greedy decode (identical trajectory ⇒ identical verify workload, isolating the GDN launch overhead): **11.0 vs 10.9 t/s, ~+1–2% e2e**, consistent across runs, never regresses. The e2e delta is small because this config is **CPU-FFN-bound** (44/64 dense FFN layers on CPU mmap); the structural win is **~4× fewer GDN-verify launches** (k=4, 48 layers: ~1824 → ~432), which matters more on GPU-FFN-resident GDN models or higher k.

author: mwiebe
body:
Bump the sfm-explorer UI-test dev-dependency from xa11y 0.8 to 0.9 and run the accessibility-driven ui_basic suite on macOS in CI alongside Windows. The two jobs are named ui-test-windows and ui-test-macos.

xa11y 0.9:
- It no longer hardcodes a 5s default timeout (unset == single attempt, no polling), so the harness sets a process-wide default before the polling locator ops (exists/press/toggle) run.
- App::by_pid now roots at the first top-level window for a pid, which on Windows is a winit helper window (a 16px "group"). Attach by window title via App::find on Windows; macOS uses by_pid (one AXApplication per process).

Make the app actually run and expose its tree off-Windows:
- The wgpu instance was hardcoded to Backends::DX12, so surface creation aborted on launch on macOS. Choose the backend per platform (DX12 / Metal / Vulkan) and enable wgpu's metal feature; Windows keeps DX12.
- run_ui_and_paint acquired the surface first and bailed on a non-presentable (occluded / off-screen) window before the egui pass that publishes the AccessKit tree. Acquire the surface after handle_platform_output, applying egui's texture deltas first so the renderer stays in sync on skipped-present frames; only the GPU submit and present are skipped.

macOS UI test specifics:
- New ui-test-macos job builds the test binary, grants it the Accessibility (TCC) permission via xa11y/setup-a11y on the exact hashed binary path, then runs it directly.
- A freshly launched app's deep widget subtree isn't queryable over the AX API for several seconds, so content lookups poll a 60s budget (5s elsewhere) and the app repaints continuously under test (gated by an env var) to keep the tree fresh. Window bounds fall back to the window element on macOS, where the AXApplication root has none.

author: jerrybecks
body:
## Bug Description

Direct visits to Japanese entry pages such as `index.ja.html`, `services.ja.html`, `about.ja.html`, and `contact.ja.html` could be redirected back to the English routes during initial page load when the browser language was English and no manual language preference had been stored.

## Root Cause

The shared language-routing scripts (`scripts/main-language.js` and `scripts/main.js`) ran initial auto-routing before checking whether the current path was already an explicit localized route. As a result, valid `.ja.html` entry pages could be overridden by automatic language detection.

## Fix

- early-return from initial language auto-routing when the current path is already an explicit `.ja.html` or `.jp.html` route
- keep the patch in both shared router files so all affected entry pages honor explicit localized URLs
- bump script cache keys on the affected Japanese entry pages so browsers load the patched router immediately

## How to Verify

1. Open `index.ja.html`, `services.ja.html`, `about.ja.html`, and `contact.ja.html` directly in a browser with an English browser locale.
2. Confirm the URL remains on the `.ja.html` route instead of redirecting to the English page.
3. Confirm the rendered page title/content is Japanese and `document.documentElement.lang` remains `ja`.

## Test Plan

- [ ] Added regression test for this bug
- [ ] Existing tests still pass
- [x] Manual verification of the fix

Manual verification completed locally on:
- `http://127.0.0.1:4173/index.ja.html?verify=jp-route-fix-v4`
- `http://127.0.0.1:4173/services.ja.html?verify=jp-route-fix-v4`
- `http://127.0.0.1:4173/about.ja.html?verify=jp-route-fix-v40`
- `http://127.0.0.1:4173/contact.ja.html?verify=jp-route-fix-v40`

## Risk Assessment

Low — the change is narrowly scoped to initial language auto-routing and only suppresses redirect behavior when the visitor is already on an explicit localized route. It does not change manual language switching behavior or non-localized route handling.

## Summary

- `fleet trends <slug>` prints three sparkline rows over the trailing 12 weeks (PRs merged/wk, $ spent/wk, send-back rate/wk) so the operator can SEE whether a trend has reversed without mentally diffing seven `fleet weekly` snapshots.
- Six modes: default three-row, `--axis prs|cost|sendbacks`, `--weeks N` (4..52), `--json`, `--all`, `--all --json`.
- Advisory footer fires ONLY on the two-axis trigger (PR velocity ↓ AND send-back rate ↑ for ≥3 consecutive weeks) — single-axis trends are noise.

## Contract affirmations

- **Pure reader, no events.jsonl writes.** AC#12 asserts every cache's `events.jsonl` + `runs.jsonl` byte-size is unchanged before and after invocation.
- **No `fleet_*` signature changes.** `lib/common.sh` untouched.
- **No runtime hot-path changes.** No `lib/ship.sh` / `lib/groom.sh` / `lib/review.sh` edits; no new event types; no `fleet_emit_event` calls from the new subcommand.
- **No `prompts/` changes.** AC#13 asserts `git diff --name-only main...HEAD -- lib/common.sh prompts/` is empty.

## Implementation notes

- Eight `trends_*` helpers + dispatcher placed ABOVE the `if [ "$CMD" = "trends" ]` block (LESSONS 2026-06-05 forward-reference trap).
- Bucket math is pure awk `(epoch - anchor) / 604800` with a Julian-day-formula `iso2ep` so the whole walk is one subprocess per slug regardless of event count (LESSONS 2026-06-15 / 2026-06-11 defended).
- `--all` over 5 fixture slugs uses < 10 `date` calls total (AC#9).
- JSON escape via `preflight_json_escape` called DIRECTLY — no `*_json_escape` wrapper (LESSONS 2026-06-13).
- Slope arrows in JSON are ASCII `up|flat|down` so downstream JSON consumers do not need UTF-8 handling (LESSONS 2026-06-08).
- Sparkline glyphs emitted via awk `printf("%s", out)` from a pre-built `glyphs[1..8]` array under explicit `LC_ALL=C` (LESSONS 2026-06-03 / 2026-06-05).
- Every code path in `trends()` ends with an explicit `exit 0` or `exit 2` (LESSONS 2026-06-01).
- Help banner block at the top of `bin/fleet` and the README "Daily ops" code block each got one new line.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC#1 — usage refusal + unknown-slug refusal (both stderr, exit 2)
- [x] AC#2 — default 12-week window via single awk pass; PRs/wk counts `pr_footer_posted`
- [x] AC#3 — three axes render; `$ spent/wk` sums `total_cost_usd`; send-back rate uses 0/0 = 0
- [x] AC#4 — sparkline encoder maps `0..7,6..3` to `▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█▇▆▅▄`; min==max collapses to all-▁
- [x] AC#5 — slope arrows ↑ / → / ↓ via ±20% band
- [x] AC#6 — advisory footer fires only on two-axis trigger
- [x] AC#7 — `--weeks 4..52` boundary enforced
- [x] AC#8 — `--axis prs|cost|sendbacks` restricts to one row
- [x] AC#9 — `--all` sorted by slope; < 10 date calls
- [x] AC#10 — `--json` shape (Node-validated); ASCII `up|flat|down`
- [x] AC#11 — `--all --json` emits array
- [x] AC#12 — pure reader; byte-size assertion
- [x] AC#13 — `lib/common.sh` + `prompts/` untouched
- [x] AC#14 — `--help` mentions slug + `--all` + `--axis` + `--weeks` + `--json`

## Test plan

- [x] `bash -n lib/*.sh bin/fleet` green

author: milanvijay6
body:
🚨 **Severity:** HIGH
💡 **Vulnerability:** Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). In `server/routes/oauth.js`, the `/callback` endpoint dynamically generated HTML responses that directly interpolated untrusted URL query parameters (like `error`, query keys, `rawUrl`) and internal error objects without escaping.
🎯 **Impact:** If an attacker crafted a malicious link containing JavaScript payloads in the query parameters (e.g., `?error=<script>alert(1)</script>`), any user clicking the link would execute the arbitrary code within the context of the application, potentially leading to session hijacking.
🔧 **Fix:** Introduced an `escapeHtml` utility function that explicitly casts inputs to strings (preventing Array bypass from duplicate query parameters) and escapes sensitive HTML characters (`<`, `>`, `&`, `"`, `'`). Applied this to `error`, `rawUrl`, `fullUrl`, `Object.keys(req.query)`, and `err.message` in all HTML responses.
✅ **Verification:** Verified syntax with `node -c server/routes/oauth.js` and confirmed the explicit mitigations via an isolated string verification test (`server/tests/oauth_verify.test.js`).

author: jafools
body:
## What

Audit **M3 / T18** — extend the existing data-retention cron (`server/src/jobs/dataRetention.js`) with a **housekeeping prune step** that trims operational tables that previously grew forever.

A new step 5 (`purgeHousekeepingTables`) runs at the end of each retention cycle, deleting rows past a conservative, env-overridable window from four unbounded tables. Cross-tenant/global tables, so each prune runs once (no per-tenant loop) and writes a single `system` audit row under the `retention.*` event namespace. A failure in one prune is caught so the others still run — matching the cycle's existing fail-soft style.

## Tables / columns / windows pruned (reviewer risk note)

| Table | Prune column | Default window | Env override | Why this column / window is safe |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `notifications` | `created_at` | **90 days** | `NOTIFICATION_RETENTION_DAYS` | Portal only ever shows the latest 30 rows, so older rows are already invisible; migration 022 explicitly intended a ~30-day auto-expire via this job. Read/unread state is irrelevant once this old. |
| `portal_login_tokens` | `expires_at` | **7 days** | `PORTAL_TOKEN_RETENTION_DAYS` | Single-use magic links (15-min TTL). Pruned only once **expired** for the window — never while still inside `expires_at`. |
| `portal_sessions` | `expires_at` | **30 days** | `PORTAL_SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS` | 30-day TTL sessions. Pruned on `expires_at` so a still-valid long-lived session is never cut short. |
| `processed_stripe_events` | `processed_at` | **90 days** | `STRIPE_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS` | Idempotency ledger from #200/#214. Stripe never retries a webhook beyond ~3 days, so a 90-day window keeps replay protection for every event Stripe could still redeliver while letting old ids drop. |

Column names verified against the CREATE TABLE in migrations `022`, `035`, `043` — not guessed.

**Not pruned:** `audit_logs` (legally retained 7 years) is deliberately excluded. The auth tokens/sessions prune on `expires_at`, never `created_at`, so rows inside their TTL are untouched.

## Safety

- All four DELETEs are `<column> < $1` with a single timestamp param — fully parameterized, no value interpolation.
- `parseRetentionDays` clamps to a **1-day floor**, so a malformed/zero/negative env value can never widen the window to 0 (which would prune live rows) or go negative.
- No migration needed: new `event_type` values (e.g. `retention.notifications_purged`, 28 chars) fit `audit_logs.event_type VARCHAR(60)`, which has no CHECK constraint.

## Tests

SQL/window logic is factored into **pure helpers** (`parseRetentionDays`, `buildHousekeepingPrunes`) so it's unit-testable without Postgres. New `tests/dataRetention.test.js` — **18 tests**, collect-then-run async runner matching `tests/engine.test.js` — asserts the exact tables, prune columns (incl. the "never `created_at` for tokens/sessions" rule), full parameterization, cutoff math against an injected `now`, env-override plumbing, the clamp floor, the Stripe-window-vs-retry-horizon invariant, and that no non-target table (`audit_logs`/`conversations`/`customers`/`messages`) ever appears. Wired into the `test` + `test:unit` npm scripts.

## Local gates

- `cd server && npm ci` — clean (236 packages, 0 vulnerabilities)
- `server` `npm run lint` (eslint .) — **clean, no errors**
- `NODE_ENV=test node tests/dataRetention.test.js` — **18 passed, 0 failed**
- Full unit suite (all 10 files) re-run individually — **all pass, no regressions**

> e2e/Playwright and integration tests need Postgres/a browser and were not run locally — relying on PR CI for those.
> Note: `npm run test:unit` cannot be invoked via `npm` on Windows (the chained `NODE_ENV=test ...` inline-env syntax fails under cmd.exe); each file was run directly with the env var instead. CI runs on Linux where the script works as-is.

Staging-only change — no tag, no deploy.

body:
## Change Description

- Add application-level Redis error budget metrics so MPP can observe user-facing Redis impact, not just infrastructure symptoms.
- Instrument `redisdegrade` guard with a `MetricsObserver` hook, emitting per-group per-workload operation counts, error classification, cache hit/miss, fallback counts, and circuit-breaker state transitions.
- Provide a Grafana dashboard (`MPP Redis Error Budget (App-Side)`) that surfaces burn rate, fallback activity, cache behavior, and breaker state during failover drills.

## Implementation Approach

- Introduced `MetricsObserver` interface in `redisdegrade` package with `SetMetricsObserver` for global registration, plus `CallWork`/`DoWork` variants that accept a workload tag.
- Created `RedisMetricsObserver` in the `observability` package implementing the interface via 7 Prometheus counter/gauge families, registered through `Suite.SetupRedisMetrics()`.
- State transition tracking on `Guard.record()` notifies the observer when circuit-breaker state changes.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/pkg/redisdegrade/ ./internal/observability/ -v` -- all 14 tests pass, including 6 new tests covering observer registration, interface satisfaction, nil safety, error classification, and end-to-end metrics endpoint exposure.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
**Assumptions**
- The `upstreamHealth` logic and caching state are strictly used for health checking, and not tightly intertwined with other CAS request handling state, making extraction safe and beneficial.
- Following the single responsibility principle, `CASHandler` manages serving files, and `UpstreamHealthChecker` manages upstream liveness.

**Alternatives Not Chosen**
- A full-blown Fetcher extraction, including `tryFetchFromSource`. This was not chosen because `tryFetchFromSource` heavily depends on the `LocalRepository` (`BeginWrite`, commit) and the actual HTTPResponseWriter, meaning an extraction would just pass along all the exact same dependencies without meaningfully decreasing coupling.
- An interface for health-checking. This was not chosen because there is currently only one implementation needed, and an interface would be premature abstraction.

**How To Pivot**
- If the original logic is preferred or if a different level of extraction is desired (e.g. `CASFetcher` handling all fetching and delegating back to `CASHandler` for caching), the files `internal/handler/handler.go` can be reverted to their previous state, and `internal/handler/health.go` can be removed.

**Next Knobs**
- Modify the `healthTTL` constant in `health.go` to change how aggressively upstreams are probed.
- Refactor `UpstreamHealthChecker` to accept its timeout configuration via options rather than hardcoding `2500*time.Millisecond`.
- Add Prometheus metrics or detailed logging hooks directly into `UpstreamHealthChecker` without bloating the main request loop in `CASHandler`.

author: wilkmar
body:
Zaza functional tests require Python 3.10, while some charm branches
require Python 3.12 to build. This means functional tests must run on
Jammy (Python 3.10), but the func runner would fail to build charms
that require Python 3.12.

To work around this, add support for building charms with uv, which
allows running the 'build' tox target with an arbitrary Python version.
The required Python version is detected from the charm repo's tox.ini
using 'tox --showconfig -e build', falling back to 3.12 on failure.

uv-based builds are currently not supported with '--remote-build'

body:
Fixes #3

### SUMMARY

Replace unsafe `yaml.load(..., Loader=yaml.Loader)` with `yaml.safe_load()` in `superset/examples/utils.py`.

`yaml.Loader` can instantiate arbitrary Python objects during deserialization, which is a code-execution risk (Bandit B506). The metadata being parsed is a simple dict with string scalars (`type`, `version`, `timestamp`), so `yaml.safe_load()` is a drop-in replacement with no functional regression.

```diff
- metadata = yaml.load(contents.get(METADATA_FILE_NAME, \"{}\"), Loader=yaml.Loader)  # noqa: S506
+ metadata = yaml.safe_load(contents.get(METADATA_FILE_NAME, \"{}\"))
```

Also adds two tests:
1. **Runtime test** — patches `yaml.safe_load` with a `wraps` spy to assert it is called with the metadata content and that the `type` key removal logic still works.
2. **Static AST test** — parses the source of `utils.py` and fails if any `yaml.load()` call is found, acting as a regression guard independent of the runtime environment.

author: hardbyte
body:
> **Draft / spike — not for merge.** Exploratory feasibility evidence for the deferred awa v0.7 segment engine ([awa#169](https://github.com/hardbyte/awa/issues/169) / [awa#197](https://github.com/hardbyte/awa/issues/197)). Posted as a PR so the design + numbers are reviewable in one place.

## What

A harness adapter (`segmented-bench/`) implementing the rotation-first storage model the original #169 spike recommended but left unproven on speed: append-only `events`/`claims`/`done` slot rings + a **Postgres-sequence dispatch cursor** (per-job claim/ack, no anti-join, no hot `UPDATE`) + `TRUNCATE`-on-rotation prune. Native Python adapter (no Docker), launched with the harness interpreter.

- **[DESIGN.md](segmented-bench/DESIGN.md)** — schema + hot paths + the pin-immunity argument.
- **[SPIKE_FINDINGS.md](segmented-bench/SPIKE_FINDINGS.md)** — full results.

## The question (from the #169 spike)

The original spike proved the claim-ledger *storage shape* collapses dead tuples but found the *naive* claim algorithm (anti-join over history) too slow (590/294 TPS). Recommendation: "a queue-local cursor/range allocator, not a global anti-join." This spike implements that and asks: **pin-immune AND fast, keeping per-job semantics?**

## Findings

- **Pin-immunity (Q2): proven.** 30-min idle-in-tx pin @ 3k/s → dead tuples flat (peak 1,527, *all* on the single rotation pointer; every append-only ring = 0). Contrast queue_storage's 130k on `queue_claim_heads`.
- **Fast claim (Q1): yes, short-burst.** Cursor allocator sustains 1–5k/s for 2–3 min with latency competitive-to-better than awa at 128 workers (e.g. 5k: 29 ms vs 161 ms p99) — ~8–17× the anti-join spike.
- **Sustained throughput: needs work.** Over 30 min it couldn't hold 3k/s (depth ran away). Partly host contention during the run (concurrent CI), partly maturity gaps: one-connection-per-worker, ~5 round-trips/claim, and prune-`TRUNCATE` contention with workers. A clean-host long-run is needed to characterize the true sustained ceiling.

## Recommendation

Open the **v0.7 segment-storage RFC** with this as feasibility evidence: the storage shape is pin-immune and a cursor allocator makes the claim path fast in bursts. The remaining work is design-first — the omitted per-job semantics (heartbeats / retries+backoff / priorities+aging / DLQ / unique / callbacks; each reintroduces mutable control state) and the maturity gaps above. Nothing here changes the 0.6 decision: this stays post-0.6, opt-in, design-first.

Refs awa#169, awa#197.

author: ojongerius
body:
## Summary

Clicking a node in the agent graph now highlights its entire **state-dependency connected component** — every agent reachable via shared-resource contention edges — instead of just the single clicked node. This makes a cross-agent contention group visible at a glance, which was awkward when several agents share resources (the one-node-at-a-time blast radius hid the broader story).

Closes #135.

## Behavior

- Clicking a node highlights the clicked node (solid accent ring) plus all peers in its state-dep component (dashed accent ring), emphasizes the in-component state-dep edges, and dims everything outside the component.
- **Delegation edges are excluded** from component computation — they connect every sub-agent through the root, which would collapse the whole graph into one component. Only `state_dep` (provable shared-resource) edges define the group.
- A node with no state-dep edges highlights only itself, preserving today's single-node behavior.
- The blast-radius panel and receipts filter remain keyed to the **clicked node** only — unchanged.
- Clicking the selected node again resets, as before.
- Applies to both the modal session graph and the receipts-view inline graph (they share `renderSessionGraphSVG`); each graph's selection is scoped to its own `<svg>`.

## Implementation

Frontend-only, in `internal/server/static/index.html`:

- New `graphComponent(startId, svg)` — BFS over `.sg-edge-state` edges only, returns the reachable node-id set.
- New `applyComponentHighlight(el)` — shared highlight coordinator scoped via `el.closest('svg')`; toggles `sg-selected`/`sg-comp` on nodes, `sg-edge-active` on edges, and `sg-has-selection` on the `<svg>`. Returns the clicked node id, or `null` on toggle-off.
- `selectGraphNode` / `selectInlineGraphNode` rewritten to delegate highlighting to the shared helper.
- State-dep edge `<path>` elements now carry `data-from` / `data-to` (escaped) so the component can be traversed from the DOM.
- CSS for the component/dimming/active-edge states.
- Hint text updated to mention the shared-resource group.

## Testing

- `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` all pass (the static file is embedded via `go:embed`).
- The frontend has no JS test runner in this repo; verified by reading the diff and the `/code-review` skill (high effort) returned no findings.

## Notes

- The dashboard remains read-only; no Go or backend changes.
- `CHANGELOG.md` updated under `[Unreleased]`.

author: serena-ruan
body:
## Problem

On #556 a maintainer applied `skip-security-scan`, but some Security Gate checks re-ran and others stayed red ([example failing run](https://github.com/omnigent-ai/omnigent/actions/runs/27739948763), [another](https://github.com/omnigent-ai/omnigent/actions/runs/27740511072)).

Root cause: the waiver required **two** events — the `skip-security-scan` label **AND** a maintainer approval (`should-scan.sh`). On #556 they arrived 8 minutes apart:

| Time | Event | Effect |
|------|-------|--------|
| 06:12 | approval | premature relay fires while the label is still missing → scan still fails → gate workflows re-run and sit **in-progress** |
| 06:20 | label applied | scan re-runs and **passes**; the decisive relay fires |
| 06:20 | relay | tries `gh run rerun` on the still-in-progress runs → GitHub rejects (`could not re-run`) → stale failing checks stick |

CI and E2E recovered because they have their own `labeled` trigger; Lint, Integration, and E2E UI depended solely on the relay and stayed red.

## Why label-only is safe

The approval half added no real authority. Applying the `skip-security-scan` label requires GitHub **Triage** permission, which on this repo is only granted to **write/admin collaborators** — a fork author can never apply one. Anyone who can apply the label can already push code to the repo, so the waiver grants no privilege they don't already have. The extra approval step bought nothing except the timing race.

## Changes

- **`should-scan.sh`** — replace `skip_label_effective()` (label + maintainer approval/author) with `has_skip_label()` (label presence only). Still fails closed on missing token/repo/PR. `author_is_maintainer` (private-membership author trust) is unchanged.
- **`security-scan.yml`** — drop the `pull_request_review` trigger; re-run on `labeled`/`unlabeled` only. Update the on-failure waiver message.
- **`rerun-security-gate.yml`** — drop the `pull_request_review` trigger; gate the record job on the skip label only.
- **`rerun-security-gate-run.yml`** — **race guard**: wait for the head SHA's `Security Scan` check to complete and only re-run gate workflows once it has passed, so the relay never churns in-progress runs.

## Validation

All four workflows + `security-gate.yml` parse as YAML; `should-scan.sh` passes `bash -n`. `shellcheck`/`actionlint` aren't installed locally — relying on CI's lint job.

## :loudspeaker: Type of change
- [ ] Bugfix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Enhancement
- [x] Refactoring


## :scroll: Description

Adds a carrier-level base64 polyfill hook (`carrier.base64Polyfill`) that mirrors the existing `encodePolyfill` indirection used for UTF-8 encoding.

- New `packages/core/src/js/transports/base64Polyfill.ts` — exposes `useBase64Polyfill()` and the default `base64Polyfill` implementation (delegates to the existing JS `base64StringFromByteArray` from `vendor/base64-js`).
- New `packages/core/src/js/utils/base64.ts` — `encodeToBase64()` helper that lazy-installs the polyfill and dispatches through the carrier.
- `wrapper.ts` (`captureEnvelope`) now calls `encodeToBase64(envelopeBytes)` instead of `base64StringFromByteArray(envelopeBytes)` directly.
- `sdk.tsx` installs the polyfill at init alongside `useEncodePolyfill()`.
- The React Native carrier type is extended locally with an optional `base64Polyfill?: (input: Uint8Array | number[]) => string` field. Upstream `@sentry/core` is not touched.

**Behavior is unchanged** — the same JS encoder runs by default. This PR is plumbing only.


## :bulb: Motivation and Context

Stage 1 of #4884. The pure-JS base64 encoder is a measurable bottleneck on the envelope hot path (`RNSentry.captureEnvelope`) for larger payloads (profiles, attachments, replays). Putting the carrier hook in place now means a future native (JSI / TurboModule) encoder can be dropped in by swapping a single carrier assignment, without touching any call sites in event-processing code.

Refs #4884.


## :green_heart: How did you test it?

- New test: `packages/core/test/transports/base64Polyfill.test.ts` — verifies the polyfill is installed on the carrier and that the default encoder produces correct base64 output.
- `yarn test` — all 1619 tests pass.
- `yarn build` — passes.
- `yarn lint:lerna` — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `yarn circularDepCheck` — no circular dependencies.
- `yarn api-report:check` — API report up to date (no public API changes).


## :pencil: Checklist
- [x] I added tests to verify changes
- [x] No new PII added or SDK only sends newly added PII if `sendDefaultPII` is enabled
- [ ] I updated the docs if needed.
- [ ] I updated the wizard if needed.
- [x] All tests passing
- [x] No breaking changes


## :crystal_ball: Next steps

Stage 2 of #4884: implement the native fast path behind the same carrier hook. Two candidates to evaluate:

1. Skip base64 entirely — pass envelope bytes across the bridge as `ArrayBuffer` via TurboModule (new-arch only; fall back to the JS polyfill on old arch).
2. Vendor a JSI base64 encoder (e.g. `react-native-quick-base64`-style) and install it as the polyfill.

author: p0dalirius
body:
### Linked Issue
Closes #11

### Root Cause
The OpenGraph node schema restricts a property value to a single primitive (string, number, or boolean) or a homogeneous array of primitives; `null`, nested objects, arrays of objects, and arrays mixing primitive types are not allowed. `IsPropertyValueValid` predated those constraints: it returned `true` for `nil`, and its `reflect.Slice` case approved any slice purely by container kind, never inspecting element types or checking homogeneity. As a result `SetProperty` would store `null`, `[]map[string]any{...}`, and mixed `[]interface{}{...}` values that are serialized into payloads BloodHound rejects at ingestion.

### Fix Description
`IsPropertyValueValid` now:
- rejects `nil` (`null` is not a valid value),
- accepts a value only if it is a primitive (string, number, boolean), and
- accepts a slice/array only if every element is a primitive and all elements share the same primitive category (string / number / boolean); empty sequences remain valid.

Element classification and homogeneity are factored into two small helpers (`primitiveCategory`, `isHomogeneousPrimitiveSequence`) so the rule reads directly off the schema's `anyOf` of primitive/array types. The existing `SetProperty` contract (panic on an invalid value) is unchanged — only the definition of "valid" is corrected.

### How Verified
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test ./...` all pass.
- Tests assert validity for primitives and homogeneous arrays (`[]string`, `[]int`, `[]bool`, empty array) and invalidity for `nil`, maps/structs/funcs/channels, arrays of objects, arrays mixing primitive types, and arrays of arrays. The `SetProperty` panic path is exercised for each newly-invalid value.

### Test Coverage
**Added / updated:** `properties/Properties_test.go` — `TestIsValidPropertyValue` and `TestSetProperty` extended with homogeneous-array valid cases and `nil` / array-of-objects / mixed-array / nested-array invalid cases; the previously-valid `nil` case was moved to the invalid set to match the schema.

### Scope of Change
- **Files changed:** `properties/Properties.go`, `properties/Properties_test.go`
- **Submodule pointer updated:** no
- **Behavioral changes outside the bug fix:** none

### Risk and Rollout
Low and local to value validation. `SetProperty(k, nil)` now panics like other invalid values (previously it stored `null`). Note the pre-existing interaction with import: `NewPropertiesFromMap` — used by `FromJSON` — calls `SetProperty`, so a `null` property value in imported JSON now triggers the same panic that nested-object values already trigger today; making the import path tolerant of schema-invalid values is a separate concern and is not changed here.

author: c9s
body:
## Summary

Running `status` (and other commands) against MySQL without `parseTime=true` in the DSN fails:

```
Error: sql: Scan error on column index 1, name "tstamp": unsupported Scan,
storing driver.Value type []uint8 into type *time.Time
```

rockhopper scans the version table's `tstamp` column into `time.Time`, which requires the go-sql-driver `parseTime=true` option. Previously users had to remember to add it to their DSN by hand.

`Open` now normalizes MySQL/TiDB DSNs to guarantee `parseTime=true`, using the driver's own `mysql.ParseDSN`/`FormatDSN` so it correctly handles existing query params, unix sockets, and missing database names.

## Design

- The normalization happens in `Open`, the single chokepoint all connection paths (`OpenWithConfig`, `OpenWithEnv`, direct) funnel through. `castDriverName` has already folded TiDB into MySQL at that point, so TiDB is covered too.
- To keep `db.go` free of a hard MySQL import (and respect the existing `no_mysql` build tag), the normalizer is registered via a hook from `driver_mysql.go`. Under `no_mysql` the hook stays nil and `Open` leaves the DSN untouched.
- An already-present `parseTime=true` is preserved; other params (e.g. `charset=utf8mb4`) are kept and `parseTime` is appended.

## Tests

`driver_mysql_test.go` (build-tagged `!no_mysql`) covers: adding `parseTime` when missing, preserving it when set, appending alongside other params, unix-socket DSNs, no-database DSNs, and the invalid-DSN error path.

Verified `go build`/`go test` pass under both the default and `-tags no_mysql` builds.

author: pmcp
body:
## What

Adds a readable, plain-language **"what happens to a robot's PR"** flow to the agent docs, describing how a leaf PR from the task-decomposition pipeline reaches merge: opens PR → tests run (one sticky status note) → **merges itself** on green / **fix-bot** retries on red / **tags you** when stuck / **new ticket** on a post-merge break.

It lives as a section at the bottom of the existing generated **`skills-and-triggers.html`** — one page, not a scattered file.

## Why it's in the generator (not hand-edited HTML)

`writeups/architecture/skills-and-triggers.html` is generated by `scripts/gen-skills-doc.mjs`, and `skills-doc.yml` CI fails if the committed file doesn't byte-match the generator output. So the section is baked into the generator as a static `CI_FLOW` constant + `.cif-*` styles — edit the copy there and re-run `node scripts/gen-skills-doc.mjs`. Hand-editing the HTML would fail `--check`.

## Commits
- `537b3f2` — first cut as a standalone diagram
- `89af3b7` — refolded into the skills page (plain language, technical terms demoted to captions) + removed the standalone

> The first commit adds a file the second removes; the granular history is honest but if you'd rather, this is a fine PR to **squash** on merge.

## Note
This is a **design sketch**, not built infrastructure — epic candidate under #249. Split out of #323 (the kassa staging fix) to keep that PR single-concern.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary
新增「定时任务调度」模块：基于 cron 表达式的后台调度器，支持任务的增删改、启停、立即执行一次，以及每次执行的成功/失败日志。栈式叠加在 PR #16 之上，建议合并顺序 #14 → #15 → #16 → 本 PR。

### 数据模型
```
sys_job(id, tenant_id, name, job_group, invoke_target, cron_expr, status,
        remark, last_run_at, next_run_at, created_at, updated_at)
sys_job_log(id, tenant_id, job_id, job_name, invoke_target, status,
            message, started_at, duration_ms, created_at)
```
- `invoke_target` 是已注册处理器的键（如 `demo:heartbeat`），由后端的处理器注册表分发执行；未注册的 target 执行时记一条失败日志。
- `status`：0=暂停、1=运行中。`next_run_at` 在创建/更新/启用时按 cron 预计算。

### 调度实现（拉取式，无需外部调度库的常驻句柄）
`cron` crate 解析六段式（含秒）表达式。调度状态完全持久化在表里，便于多实例与测试：
```rust
// service::job
pub async fn tick_due_jobs(&self) -> AppResult<usize> {
    let now = Utc::now();
    let due = Job::find()
        .filter(Status.eq(1))
        .filter(NextRunAt.lte(now))   // NULL 自动排除
        .all(&db).await?;
    for job in due {
        self.execute_job(&job).await;             // 写 sys_job_log
        active.last_run_at = Set(Some(now));
        active.next_run_at = Set(next_fire_after(&job.cron_expr, now));  // 推进
    }
}
// 后台 loop：每 5s tick 一次，main.rs 启动时 tokio::spawn(run_scheduler(...))
```
- 手动「立即执行」走同一个 `execute_job`，与调度共用日志落库逻辑，但不改动 `next_run_at`。
- 非法 cron 表达式在创建/更新时即返回 400（`next_fire_after` 解析失败）。

### 接口（RBAC，`system:job:*`）
`GET/POST /api/v1/jobs`、`GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/jobs/{id}`、`PUT /api/v1/jobs/{id}/status`(启停)、`POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/run`(执行一次)、`GET /api/v1/job-logs`(可按 `job_id`/`status` 过滤)。迁移建表 + 种子一个默认暂停的示例任务 + 平台菜单池菜单 120-126 并授予 demo admin。

### 前端 `/jobs`
任务列表（行内 Switch 启停、立即执行、查看执行日志弹窗、编辑、删除），任务对话框（处理器下拉 + cron 输入 + 启用开关）。新增 `jobApi`、`Job`/`JobLog` 类型、5 个权限常量，并把 `system:job:list` 接入动态菜单。

## 验证
- `cargo fmt --check`、`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`、`cargo test -p server --lib` 全绿。
- 全量集成测试 **15/15** 通过（全新库），新增 `job_create_run_and_logs`：创建暂停任务 → 非法 cron 返回 400 → 启用后 `next_run_at` 计算 → 立即执行产生成功日志 → 按 job_id 查日志 → 删除。
- 前端 `npm run lint`、`npm run build` 通过。

author: itxaiohanglover
body:
## Summary

- `d3.select("svg")` returns the first `<svg>` in document order, which is a 16px legend icon — not the main `#graph-svg` canvas. This caused the entire force graph to render inside the tiny legend swatch while the full-screen canvas stayed empty.
- Fix: target `#graph-svg` by id in both template copies (full mode + aggregated/community mode).
- Added `id="graph-svg"` to the aggregated-view template's `<svg>` element (it was missing).

## Root cause

In `visualization.py`, the legend `<nav>` is emitted *before* `#graph-svg` and its first child is an inline `<svg>` icon:

```html
<svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="-8 -8 16 16" aria-hidden="true">...</svg>
```

`d3.select("svg")` matches this 16px icon, so `gRoot` + all nodes/links get appended into it (viewBox `-8 -8 16 16`), producing a microscopic graph in the legend and an empty canvas.

## Fix

```js
// Before
var svg = d3.select("svg").attr("viewBox", [0, 0, W, H]);

// After
var svg = d3.select("#graph-svg").attr("viewBox", [0, 0, W, H]);
```

Applied to both template copies. The aggregated-view template's `<svg>` also gets `id="graph-svg"` added (it was missing).

## Test plan

- [x] `test_generate_html_uses_id_selector_for_svg` — verifies full-mode HTML uses `d3.select("#graph-svg")` and contains no bare `d3.select("svg")`
- [x] `test_community_mode_uses_id_selector_for_svg` — verifies community-mode HTML uses `d3.select("#graph-svg")`, has no bare `d3.select("svg")`, and the `<svg>` has `id="graph-svg"`
- [x] All 22 existing visualization tests still pass
- [x] `ruff check` passes

Closes #523

body:
## Phase 2: cut every relying party over to Authelia

Authelia is deployed, healthy, and externally reachable at `https://auth.k12n.com` (phase 1, #96–#98). This PR repoints every app at the single Authelia issuer and wires the new client secrets. **Authentik stays running** as a fallback; teardown is a separate follow-up PR after per-client verification.

### Config repoints
Per-provider Authentik issuers collapse to one Authelia issuer:
- **homelab-api / homelab-settings-api** — single issuer with JWKS + introspection
- **energy-ws** — single issuer, JWKS-only (its clients issue JWT access tokens)
- **heatpump-web** — SPA base URL + `oauth.ts` endpoint paths rewritten to Authelia (`/api/oidc/authorization|token|userinfo`); `offline_access` added so Authelia issues a refresh token; logout reworked (Authelia has no OIDC end-session endpoint)
- **oauth2-proxy** (+ claude-mcp variant) — issuer URL, `offline_access` scope
- **backstage** — OIDC discovery metadata URL
- **homelab-chat-api** — issuer + token URL; scopes drop `openid`/`profile` (Authelia forbids them for the `client_credentials` grant)

### Secrets
New Authelia client secrets, sealed on-cluster:
- fresh: `homelab-api-introspection`, `homelab-settings-api-introspection`
- single-key reseal via `kubeseal --raw` (other keys untouched): oauth2-proxy, oauth2-proxy-claude-mcp, backstage `AUTH_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`, homelab-chat-api `AGENT_CLIENT_SECRET`

### Verified before cut-over
Against the live Authelia: discovery doc, a `client_credentials` token for `homelab-chat-agent` with custom scopes, and cross-client introspection by `homelab-api-backend` — all correct.

### After merge (I'll drive)
1. **heatpump-web image rebuild** — `oauth.ts` changed, so CI rebuilds the SPA image; I'll restart the deployment to pick it up. Brief login window on that one app until then.
2. Restart the repointed deployments to load new config/secrets.
3. Verify each client logs in against Authelia.
4. Then open the teardown PR (remove Authentik + dropped drift clients).

### Notes
- `redpanda-console` (oidc disabled) and `traefikoidc` (no consumer in-repo) are dormant — their Authelia clients exist but no app repoint was needed.
- `oauth2-proxy-claude-mcp` targets the untunneled `api.k12n.com` and is effectively dormant; issuer repointed for hygiene.

author: lnkuiper
body:
This PR adds a local-file debug delay that can be used to test async IO on a local machine. I've used this setting to identify and fix bottlenecks in the `COPY TO` implementation.

## Debug Local File System Delay

This new setting, `debug_local_file_system_delay_ms`, has a default value of `0`. When enabled, the Unix local file system sleeps before open/read/write operations, which can be used as a proxy for a remote file system.

When `debug_local_file_system_delay_ms > 0`, `AsyncFileWriter::IsLocalFile()` returns `false`. This makes delayed local writes use the same coalescing behavior as remote writes, which is important for the proxy: otherwise the local writer path still behaves too differently from remote files even though each local operation sleeps. I considered making `FileSystem::IsRemoteFile()` return `true` when this setting is activated but I thought that might be too invasive.

## Async COPY File Lifecycle

This PR also changes `COPY TO` so file initialization and finalization can run on the async task scheduler instead of blocking regular threads.

The main change is that file state creation is split into two phases:

1. A lock-held reservation phase records the output path, created-file metadata, partition values, written-file info, and stats state.
2. An async lifecycle phase runs `copy_to_initialize_global`, initializes the writer state, and later runs `copy_to_finalize`.

`FileStateHandle` is the shared object between those phases. A handle can reference either a pending open job or a ready `GlobalFileState`, and call sites use `EnsureFileStateReady` when they actually need the writer state. Finalization uses the same lifecycle executor and waits for a pending open before finalizing the file.

The lifecycle executor uses `TaskExecutor(context, TaskSchedulerType::ASYNC)`, bounds the number of queued lifecycle tasks, records the first exception, and lets waiters help drain lifecycle work (if things aren't ready or if work has built up). Query finalization and result production call `WaitForLifecycleTasks()` so returned file/stats information and temporary-file renames only happen after all async open/finalize work has completed.

The life cycle implementation is shared by all write paths, regardless of the files being remote, partitioned, etc. Partitioned file-state publication happens under the partition/global locks, while scheduling and finalization are done after releasing those locks.

There is something to be said about these tasks being scheduled on async threads even though they do more than just IO. I think this is necessary because we're calling opaque callbacks that can be implemented in extensions. This PR achieves asynchronous behaviour cleanly without modifying extensions/callbacks.

## Results / Benchmarks

These are runs on my laptop with TPC-H SF 10 with `debug_local_file_system_delay_ms=1` and `SET threads=8;`.

| Query | Execution Time [s] |
| --- | ---: |
| `PARTITION_BY (l_quantity)` (~50 partitions) | 6.51 |
| `PARTITION_BY (l_shipdate)` (~2.5k partitions) | 8.65 |
| `PARTITION_BY (l_suppkey)` (~100k partitions) | 8.63 |
| Single parquet file | 3.87 |
| `FILE_SIZE_BYTES '32MiB'` (62 files) | 3.70 |

Without the life cycle changes or with `async_threads=0`, all of these queries could take 20 to 30 seconds.

## Summary

body:
## Summary Moves the dashboard widget cache work out of PR #29177 into a separate stacked PR. This keeps the shell/lazy-loading changes independently mergeable while the cache/SWR behavior can be reviewed or skipped separately. Ref: https://github.com/open-metadata/openmetadata-collate/issues/4230 ## Changes - Adds a bounded LRU cache helper and useDashboardWidgetData hook. - Applies stale-while-revalidate style cache reuse to My Data dashboard widgets. - Adds focused unit coverage for cache reuse, request coalescing, disabled state, and cache clearing. ## Tests - ./node_modules/.bin/jest src/hooks/useDashboardWidgetData.test.ts src/components/MyData/RightSidebar/FollowingWidget.test.tsx src/components/MyData/Widgets/TotalDataAssetsWidget/TotalDataAssetsWidget.test.tsx --runInBand --no-coverage

Greptile Summary

 This PR introduces a stale-while-revalidate caching layer for My Data dashboard widgets by adding a bounded LRU cache utility, a `useDashboardWidgetData` hook with request coalescing and epoch-based invalidation, and migrating five widgets off their own local `useState`/`useEffect` fetch loops. - **New `lruCacheUtils.ts` + `useDashboardWidgetData` hook**: Module-level LRU cache (50-entry cap) with a `clearDashboardWidgetCache()` function that increments an epoch to prevent in-flight requests from re-populating the cache after logout. Request coalescing is handled via a shared `Map>`. - **Widget migrations**: `MyDataWidget`, `FollowingWidget`, `DataAssetsWidget`, `TotalDataAssetsWidget`, and `KPIWidget` all replace their local state/effect fetch patterns with the new hook. `DataAssetsWidget` incidentally gains a previously missing `selectedSortBy` dependency on its fetcher. - **Test coverage**: `useDashboardWidgetData.test.ts` adds focused unit tests for cache reuse, request coalescing, disabled state, and cache clearing; component tests are updated with `clearDashboardWidgetCache()` in `beforeEach`.

Confidence Score: 3/5

 The caching infrastructure is well-structured and the widget migrations are clean, but the epoch guard in useDashboardWidgetData incompletely covers the logout/user-switch scenario it was explicitly designed for. The core of the PR — the LRU utility, the hook's coalescing logic, and all five widget migrations — is sound. However, the epoch mechanism that is supposed to prevent a previous user's in-flight data from reaching the new user's UI only guards the cache write and not the React state write (setData), so stale data can still render in same-session user-switch flows. The gap is small in code terms (one line needs moving inside the guard) but the comment directly above it promises this case is handled. useDashboardWidgetData.ts — the setData(response) call at line 100 needs to move inside the epoch === dashboardWidgetCacheEpoch guard.

Security Review

 - **Stale user data after logout** (`useDashboardWidgetData.ts` line 100): The epoch guard prevents writing old data back to the module-level cache on user switch, but `setData(response)` is unconditional — if a component is still mounted when a logout flushes the cache and a prior user's in-flight request resolves afterward, that user's data is written into React state and rendered for the new session.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | openmetadata-ui/src/main/resources/ui/src/hooks/useDashboardWidgetData.ts | New SWR-style hook with request coalescing and epoch-based cache invalidation. The epoch guard correctly prevents re-populating the module-level cache after logout, but setData(response) is unconditional — stale previous-user data can still be written to React component state when an in-flight request resolves after a cache clear. | | openmetadata-ui/src/main/resources/ui/src/utils/lruCacheUtils.ts | New bounded LRU cache backed by Map insertion-order; get() correctly promotes keys, set() evicts LRU on overflow, clear/delete are correct. Implementation is clean and well-documented. | | openmetadata-ui/src/main/resources/ui/src/constants/DashboardCache.constants.ts | Adds three cache-size constants; only MAX_DASHBOARD_WIDGET_CACHE_ENTRIES is consumed in this PR. The other two are forward declarations for future caches. | | openmetadata-ui/src/main/resources/ui/src/components/MyData/Widgets/KPIWidget/KPIWidget.component.tsx | Refactored to use three chained useDashboardWidgetData calls (kpiList → kpiResults/kpiLatestResults, enabled when kpiList is non-empty). The cascade is correct; loading state is now the union of all three, which is accurate. | | openmetadata-ui/src/main/resources/ui/src/hooks/useDashboardWidgetData.test.ts | New focused unit tests covering SWR cache reuse, request coalescing, disabled state, and cache clearing. Deferred-promise helpers enable precise async control. |

Sequence Diagram

author: bbfox0703
body:
Adds a second-stage GWorld recovery and fixes the recovery-mode UI signalling. DLL + C# UI. In-game path-verified on SEED (UE4.27).

## What

**1. `Genau::RecoverGWorldViaEngine` (`engine_recovery`)** — gap-fill chained after `ExtraScanGWorld`. When no static `.data` slot points at the live UWorld, recover via the engine object graph: GEngine → GameViewport → `&World` (the address of the live `UWorld*` field inside `UGameViewportClient`, which the engine updates on level loads). A single deref yields the current world, so every GWorld consumer (teleport / live walk / path search) works unchanged. GEngine is identified by a reflected `GameViewport` member (version-independent, per-class cached), not a class name; the `World` offset comes from reflection with a bounded memory-probe fallback.

> Known limit (by design): the recovered slot is a heap object field, not a static module symbol — valid for live ops but not for cross-session CE symbol export. The gap case has no static anchor to export anyway, which is why the AOB symbol toggle is force-disabled.

**2. AOB-toggle gating fix** — recovery now nulls `g_cachedGWorldAob`/`Pos`/`Len` (and `g_cachedGWorldScanAddr`) on every branch, so the Live Walker "AOB" GWorld-symbol checkbox auto-unchecks + grays out and the Pointers-panel `AOB: <scan addr>` row hides. Also fixes the same latent bug in the pre-existing `instance_scan_recovery` path.

**3. Pointers-panel clarity** — GWorld now shows its recovery method (`⚠ AOB failed — found via engine recovery`), mirroring GObjects/GNames; previously GWorld had no method display, so a recovered GWorld read like a normal AOB hit. `FormatMethodLabel` gains friendly arms for the recovery methods.

**4. Test hook** — game-process env `UE5DUMP_FORCE_GWORLD_RECOVERY=1` forces the full recovery chain; `=engine` skips `ExtraScanGWorld` to drive the new engine path directly. Non-destructive on failure.

## Safety
Strictly gated (only when `*GWorld` doesn't deref to a UWorld AND `Aura::GetCount()>0`), so titles with a correct GWorld are byte-identical — zero regression.

## Verification
- 620 DLL tests + 1592 C# tests green; AOT publish clean (46.3 MB).
- In-game on SEED (UE4.27): `=engine` forced it → `GWorld recovered via engine_recovery -> 0x1AD56145F78` (heap `&viewport.World` slot); Pointers panel shows the method, no scan-addr row; Live Walker AOB checkbox grayed.

## What

Add a path to the `provision-skills-telemetry` skill: when a ready `env` file (with `SKILLS_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT` and `SKILLS_TELEMETRY_TOKEN`) is provided, the skill copies it verbatim into the config dir instead of provisioning field by field. Bump the package to 1.6.0.

Supports importing a pre-filled config file. The skill is told not to open, read, or echo the file, so a token never enters the model context — `cp` moves the bytes without reading them. The two properties are enough; the CLI mints the anonymous `machine-id` itself on first send.

author: sankalpaacharya
body:
## What

Turns the MCP into a **hosted product**: clients connect to `https://keyloom.app/api/mcp` by URL with a keyloom API key — no repo clone, no local AWS creds — instead of running the stdio server locally.

## How it fits together

```
/account (WorkOS AuthKit) → sign in → mint API key (kl_live_…)
Claude/Cursor → https://keyloom.app/api/mcp  (Authorization: Bearer kl_live_…)
   → verify key (Neon) → subscription active? under quota? → run tools
   render_component → start Lambda render → count 1 against quota
   get_render_status → poll → presigned MP4 url
```

## Included

- **Data layer** — Neon Postgres + Drizzle: `users`, `subscriptions`, `api_keys` (schema pushed to Neon). Client over Neon serverless HTTP driver.
- **Auth** — WorkOS AuthKit for the dashboard (`middleware.ts`, `/callback`, `withAuth`). `/account` page: sign in, mint/revoke API keys (full secret shown once, stored hashed), and see plan + render usage. Free tier auto-provisioned on first sign-in.
- **API keys** — `kl_live_…` keys, SHA-256 hashed at rest; `authenticateApiKey` resolves a key to its owner + subscription.
- **Hosted MCP route** — `app/api/[transport]/route.ts` via `mcp-handler` over HTTP, gated by Bearer API key (`withMcpAuth`). Tools: `list_components`, `get_component_schema`, `render_component`, `get_render_status`. Per-plan render quota enforced atomically.
- **Async render** — `features/mcp` render split into `startRender` + `getRenderStatus` so the serverless route never blocks; blocking `renderComponent` kept for the stdio server.

## Not in this PR (next)

- **Dodo billing** — checkout route + `/api/webhooks/dodo` that flips subscription status/quota and provisions keys. The API-key gate + quota are already in place for it to drive.

## Env required (set in Vercel for deploy)

`DATABASE_URL`, `WORKOS_API_KEY`, `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID`, `WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI` (add `https://keyloom.app/callback` in the WorkOS dashboard), plus the existing `REMOTION_*` render vars. `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` controls the MCP URL shown on /account.

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit` ✓, `biome ci` ✓ on all new files, full `next build` ✓ (174 pages).
- Schema applied to Neon via `drizzle-kit push`.
- Not yet exercised end-to-end against a live MCP client / WorkOS sign-in — worth a manual pass once deployed with the WorkOS redirect URI configured.

author: saxon134
body:
Automated implementation for issue #60.

Issue summary:
`doStream` always calls `do` with `requestTimeoutDisabled`, and `do` only applies `WithTimeout`/`WithRequestTimeout` when the mode is `requestTimeoutUntilBodyClosed`. As a result, `Chat.Stream` and task event streams can wait forever for response headers when using the default `http.Client`, even if the SDK default timeout or a per-request timeout is configured. Apply the timeout until the stream response is established, then avoid canceling the context used for the response body, or expose/document a separate streaming timeout behavior.

File: `request.go`

Line: 108

author: tr5k-agent
body:
## Summary
Makes Claude Code's `/login` + onboarding state survive pod restarts for the devbox-claude agent.

**Background:** Claude Code keeps state in two places — `~/.claude/` (credentials, sessions) and `~/.claude.json` (a dotfile directly under `$HOME` holding the onboarding-complete flag, trusted-folder decision, and oauth account). Mounting a PVC at `~/.claude` persists the first but not the second, so a restarted pod re-shows the setup prompt. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` does **not** relocate `~/.claude.json`, so the only way to persist it is to make `$HOME` itself persistent.

**Why set HOME in the boot script (not the Agent's pod-wide env):** a pod-wide `HOME` (`podSpec.extraEnv`) is injected into the `git-init` sidecars too, which don't have the persistence volume mounted — so it breaks their git auth (`failed to setup authentication: exit status 255`, observed). `git-init` never runs this boot script, so setting `HOME` here scopes it to the server container only; git-init keeps `HOME=/tmp`.

- Sets `export HOME=/home/claude` (+ `mkdir -p`) before launching Claude Code.
- **Contract:** a consuming Agent CR mounts its persistence PVC at `/home/claude`. Without one it's just an ephemeral dir (no persistence, no breakage).

Pairs with a k3s-config-private bundle change (mount the `claude-home` PVC + `~/.tmux.conf` at `/home/claude`, drop the pod-wide `HOME` env) once a new candidate digest is cut from this.

## Test plan
- [ ] `bash -n` passes (done).
- [ ] After a candidate cut + bundle repin: pod boots (git-init auth OK), `echo $HOME` in the server container → `/home/claude`.
- [ ] `/login`, restart the pod → returns logged in, no setup prompt (`~/.claude/.credentials.json` and `~/.claude.json` both present under `/home/claude`).

author: gerry-cern
body:
## Summary

Implements the **ownCloud Web** side of ADR-0005 hierarchical sharing conflicts for collaborator share mutations via Graph.

When Reva rejects a create/update share with **HTTP 409** and a structured JSON body, the UI:

- Shows an **error** for hard conflicts (`parent_conflict`, `can_force: false`)
- Shows a **confirmation dialog** for warnings (`child_conflict`, `can_force: true`)
- **Retries the same mutation** with the `Force: true` header after the user confirms

**Backend contract:** targets Jesse Geens' Reva branch [`feat/share-consistency`](https://github.com/cs3org/reva/pull/5562). Deploy **web and Reva together**.

### Behaviour

| Mutation | Entry point | Conflict handling |
|----------|-------------|-------------------|
| **Create** (invite) | `InviteCollaboratorForm` | Deferred batch: collect all `child_conflict` 409s during parallel invites, show **one** combined modal, then re-issue failed invites with `Force: true` |
| **Update** | `ListItem` (role/expiry) | Per-action confirm modal → retry with `Force: true` |
| **Delete** | `FileShares`, `SpaceMembers` | Same retry wrapper (latent until Reva exposes hierarchy 409 on DELETE) |

### Reva JSON contract (409)

```json
{
  "error_type": "parent_conflict | child_conflict",
  "message": "...",
  "can_force": true,
  "conflicting_shares": [{ "id", "resource_id", "path", "permission_type" }]
}

author: vampik33
body:
## What

M2 PR3 (deployer render). The bundle-less K8s worker (`greentic-start start --env <id>`) pulls its `.gtbundle` at boot — greenticai/greentic-start#278 — when a routed revision carries a `bundle_source_uri`. But the rendered NetworkPolicies leave the worker **DNS-only on egress** (`gtc-default-deny` denies the rest), so under a NetworkPolicy-enforcing CNI (Calico/Cilium — the production posture) the pull fails closed.

kind's default CNI does **not** enforce NetworkPolicy, so the kind E2E can't catch this — it's a render-side **production-correctness** concern, covered by unit tests here.

## Change

`render_network_policies` now appends a gated `gtc-allow-worker-egress` policy (allow-all egress, worker pods only) **when the env routes a revision with a `bundle_source_uri`**.

- **Allow-all egress** is acceptable: the pull is integrity-gated against the revision's `bundle_digest`, so egress breadth is not a pack-injection vector. A per-destination allow-list is a tracked hardening follow-up.
- **Gated**: a probe-only env (no pullable routed revision) keeps the tighter default-deny posture — env-level object count stays 10 there, 11 only when a revision is pullable.
- The gate mirrors greentic-start's routed-only boot pull: an unrouted revision with a source uri does **not** open egress.

## Deferred (documented in the diff)

- **registry-base env vars** (`GREENTIC_REPO/STORE_REGISTRY_BASE`) — unneeded for digest-pinned `oci://` refs; wire when a `repo://`/`store://` flow lands.
- **explicit writable-cache env** — the OCI fetch + archive extract already land on M1's writable HOME and `/tmp` emptyDirs.

## Tests

- egress rendered iff a routed revision is pullable
- an unrouted pullable revision does not open egress
- a pullable env renders exactly one extra env-level object
- `bundle_source_uri` survives the env-store ConfigMap round-trip (what the worker boot seam reads)

`bash ci/local_check.sh` green (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, all lib tests, no-default-features build). Includes a `cargo update` lockfile refresh (`bytes` patch + a transitive `greentic-deploy-spec` registry bump; the deployer's own lib uses the path member, unaffected).

## Follow-up

PR4 (kind E2E): in-cluster/public registry + a pushed bundle, asserting the worker pulls → materializes → serves a real revision Ready.

body:
💡 **What:** Replaced the `.map().filter()` chain and array spreading in `orderMatchesSearchTerms` with a single, efficient `for` loop to populate `searchableFields`.

🎯 **Why:** The previous implementation created multiple intermediate arrays (one from the `.map()` and one from array spreading) which is inefficient, especially when processing large numbers of orders or orders with many items. Using a single `for` loop avoids these intermediate allocations, reducing memory overhead and CPU cycles.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** 
Ran a benchmark over 10,000 orders (10 items each), executing the search check 100 times:
* Baseline: `758.11 ms`
* Optimized: `606.79 ms`
* Change: A roughly `20%` performance improvement in the hot path.

author: gilbert09
body:
Ports the desktop **Steer & Queue messaging modes** (#2663) to the React Native / Expo mobile app.

## What this adds

A per-task **messaging mode** toggle controlling what happens when you send a message while a session turn is still running:

- **Queue** (default): messages are held locally while a turn is running, then flushed as a single combined prompt — in the order they were typed — once the turn ends.
- **Steer**: the message interrupts the running turn and is resent right away. Mobile is cloud-only and has no native mid-turn inject, so Steer maps to **interrupt-and-resend** (cancel the live turn via the existing cloud `cancel` command, then resend as a fresh prompt).

## Changes

- **`messagingModeStore`** — persisted per-task mode override plus a global default (defaults to Queue), mirroring the desktop store but using the app's `zustand + persist + AsyncStorage` pattern.
- **`messageQueueStore`** — lightweight in-memory queue with `enqueue` / `drain` / `prepend` and a pure `combineQueuedMessages` helper (FIFO order preserved, attachments concatenated).
- **`taskSessionStore`** — a single `sendInterrupting` chokepoint for interrupt-and-resend, and an auto-flush that drains the queue when a turn ends. Failed flushes roll the messages back onto the head of the queue.
- **`TaskChatComposer`** — a touch-friendly toggle pill showing the current mode and the queued count (`Queue (3)`).
- **Settings** — a global "Messaging mode" default.
- **Analytics** — sends emit a `Prompt sent` event carrying `is_steer`.

All changes are confined to `apps/mobile`; no desktop or shared package code is touched.

## Testing

- Unit tests for the mode store (override vs global default resolution) and the queue store (FIFO ordering, drain-clears, failed-flush rollback ordering, combine ordering).
- `vitest run` — 41 files / 280 tests pass.
- Typecheck and Biome lint clean on the touched files.

author: aruneshdwivedi
body:
When a TLS secret contains a certificate chain where the leaf certificate is expired but the intermediate CA is still valid, `filterValidCertificates` was filtering out only the expired leaf. The remaining chain (intermediate CA only) was passed to Envoy, which then rejected it with KEY_VALUES_MISMATCH because the private key belongs to the leaf, not the CA.

This fix checks if the first PEM block (the leaf) is expired. If it is, the entire chain is rejected -- same as if all certs were expired.

Fixes #9225

author: pal-tamas
body:
## Summary
Fixes the WASM root cause behind the dialog auto-focus race, and deduplicates the host JS-interop plumbing into `Rask.Core`.

**The fix.** WASM dispatched every `IJSRuntime` call immediately, so interop issued *during* a render — e.g. `OnRenderedAsync` focusing a `<dialog>` as it opens — ran **before** that render's DOM patch, and `focus()` hit a still-`display:none` element and silently no-op'd. Such **mid-render** calls now ride the render frame's `jsInvokes` and the client runs them **after `applyDiff`**, against the committed DOM — the post-commit ordering the Server already had. Interop from **event handlers** still dispatches immediately on WASM (the path awaited handler interop, e.g. `CodeSample`'s clipboard copy, relies on — deferring it deadlocked the awaiting handler).

The split is by `LiveRenderContext.IsActive`: mid-render → queue onto the frame (shared by both hosts); outside a render → host's existing path (Server queues + its mid-await pump flushes; WASM dispatches immediately).

**The dedup (per request).** The previously-duplicated interop logic now lives once in Core, composed by both hosts through a shared `ILiveJsHost` seam:
- `LiveJsInvokeQueue` — the pending-invoke queue (enqueue/drain/fail).
- `RaskJSRuntimeBase` — `BeginInvokeJS` deferral + the `[JSInvokable]` result envelope.
- `applyFrameInvokes` — the after-`applyDiff` dispatch loop, in the shared `rask-dom.js` (spliced into both clients), replacing the copy in `rask.js` and `rask.wasm.js`.

> A deeper follow-up (merging the full `LiveSession`/`WasmLiveSession` render/diff/payload pipeline into a shared Core base) is intentionally **staged** — the two hosts have genuinely divergent I/O models (WS push vs in-process request/response), so it warrants its own verified PR.

## Testing
- Unit: `dotnet test Rask.slnx --filter "FullyQualifiedName!~Rask.Examples.E2E"` — all pass (Server 170, WASM 46, Core 1529, …).
- E2E (`samples/` touched): hosts **Server + Wasm + StandaloneWasm** — all pass (3/3, 54s). The Todos step now asserts the dialog **auto-focuses on open** (`ToBeFocused`) then **Escape closes** it, with no prior click — on every host. (An earlier full-defer attempt regressed `CodeSample` copy on WASM; the hybrid above fixes it, confirmed by this run.)

## Benchmarks
Dispatch hot-path (`WsDispatchBenchmarks`), Allocated before → after — **zero delta**:
- SingleFragment 592 B → 592 B · 104 B → 104 B
- FourFragments 760 B → 760 B · 216 B → 216 B

## CHANGELOG
- [Unreleased] **Fixed**: WASM runs render-time `IJSRuntime` calls after the DOM patch.
- [Unreleased] **Changed**: host JS-interop plumbing shared from `Rask.Core`.

author: amourao
body:
`UpdateVectorIndexConfig` and `UpdateVectorIndexConfigs` currently mark the whole shard `READONLY` for the duration of the config update (rejecting object writes and halting LSM flush/compaction), restoring `READY` via the index callback. This removes that marking, so a vector-index config update no longer blocks writes.

### Why this is reasonable
- Cheap config changes (`ef`, dynamic-ef, `flatSearchCutoff`, cache size, filter strategy) are atomic field swaps already safe under concurrent search/insert — their read-only window is microseconds.
- In async-indexing mode the callback fires immediately and the rebuild is deferred to the queue (with its own pause), so the window is already microseconds.
- The only costly window is **sync-indexing + compression-enable**, where the rebuild otherwise holds the shard `READONLY` for minutes.

### Dependency (satisfied — no rebase needed)
- #11597 — *guard insert-path compression-state reads under compressActionLock.* Without it, removing this guard would let a concurrent multivector `AddMultiBatch` race a compression rebuild. With it, every vector writer takes `compressActionLock.RLock`, so writers **block on** (rather than race) the rebuild.
- It is **already merged on `main` and already an ancestor of this branch** (base is post-#11597), so the guard chain is present in this PR as-is: the writer swaps the compression trio under `compressActionLock.Lock()` (`compress.go:29` → `compress.go:153-154`); every insert/grow/preload reader holds `compressActionLock.RLock()` (`addOne` at `insert.go:418`, batch grow at `insert.go:170`, `AddMultiBatch` preload at `insert.go:360-366`); and the lock-free `growIndexToAccomodateNode` (`maintenance.go:42`) is only reachable under an ancestor `RLock`.

### Behavioral change: concurrent config updates serialize instead of fast-failing
Removing the READONLY window changes how a **second** config update to the **same** vector index behaves while a first one's compression rebuild is still in flight.

- The costly path is sync-indexing + enabling compression on a not-yet-compressed, cache-prefilled index. There, the rebuild runs in a background goroutine that holds `compressActionLock` (write lock) for the full train+preload duration (`compress.go`), which can be minutes.
- The first update's FSM `Apply` still returns immediately (the rebuild is dispatched async via `GoWrapper`). But a second update to the same index now **blocks** at `config_update.go:125` — where `UpdateUserConfig` takes `compressActionLock.Lock()` to swap the PQ/SQ/BQ/RQ config structs — until the first rebuild releases the lock.
- Because RAFT applies schema log entries serially, a blocked `Apply` stalls subsequent schema operations on that node until it returns.
- **Pre-PR**, that second update instead fast-failed through the `isReadOnly()` guard with a quick `422 store is read-only`. **Post-PR** it eventually succeeds (`200`, state converges). This is a correctness improvement, but downstream tooling that expects the `422` will see a latency/semantics delta.
- **Scope / mitigation:** `compressActionLock` is per-index, so this only serializes updates to the *same* index on the *same* shard; async-indexing mode returns early without compressing, so the window doesn't exist there. This is intended behavior, not a regression — verified empirically in the QA run (9/9 `200` under concurrent updates vs. baseline's 8/9 `422`). If FSM-`Apply` latency under hammered concurrent updates becomes a concern, a follow-up could make `UpdateUserConfig` non-blocking on an in-progress compress (`TryLock` / return-busy).

### Residual considerations
- LSM object writes + flush/compaction now run during a compression rebuild. This is safe: the rebuild's training reads come from `h.cache`, falling through to the objects bucket via the same consistent view (`GetObjectsBucketView` + `flushLock.RLock`) that every `Get`/search uses, and compressed vectors persist to a separate bucket (`vectors_compressed[_<target>]`). Changing the object set mid-rebuild only affects training-sample membership, not correctness.
- Reader paths (`Get`/`Stats`/search distancer closures) were never gated by the shard `READONLY` status, so their behavior is unchanged; where they read the compression trio they do so under `compressActionLock.RLock` (search/delete) or via the atomic `h.compressed` flag.
- `statusReasonVectorIndexUpdate` is no longer set by any path — the constant has been removed and the recovery-filter tests re-pointed at `statusReasonManualUpdate`. The resource-recovery discriminator still applies to other read-only reasons (resource pressure, manual, shutdown).

Base: `main`.
